definition_zh: 问；询问；请求；要求；邀请；要价
definition_en: to put a question, to request something, to invite someone, or to name a price
core_image: 一个人张开嘴，把问题递到对方面前
scene: 他在柜台前站了一会儿，终于开口。She asked the assistant where the lift was.
sceneCN: 这里 ask 是「询问」（第 1 个义项：提出问题以求回答）；句意是她问店员电梯在哪里。

derivatives.zh: 名词：请求；要价（如 asking price）

senses.title: To put a question
senses.definition: to say something in order to get an answer
senses.definitionCN: 为得到回答而说出某个问题
senses.example: She asked the assistant where the lift was.
senses.exampleCN: 她问店员电梯在哪里。
senses.why: Old English ascian meant 'to ask, to inquire', and this has stayed the word's centre.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 ascian 意为「问、打听」，这一直是这个词的核心。

senses.title: To request
senses.definition: to say that one wants something done or given
senses.definitionCN: 说出希望某事被做或被给予
senses.example: He asked for a glass of water.
senses.exampleCN: 他要了一杯水。
senses.why: A request is a question about another person's will, so the same verb covers both.
senses.whyCN: 请求本质上是在探问对方的意愿，所以同一个动词兼指两者。

senses.title: To invite
senses.definition: to tell someone you would like them to come
senses.definitionCN: 告诉某人你希望他来
senses.example: They asked us to dinner on Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们请我们周五去吃晚饭。
senses.why: An invitation asks whether a person will come, which is why ask alone can mean invite.
senses.whyCN: 邀请就是在问对方是否愿意来，所以单用 ask 也能表示邀请。

senses.title: To name a price
senses.definition: to state the amount one wants for something sold
senses.definitionCN: 说出出售某物所希望的价钱
senses.example: They are asking too much for that old car.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆旧车他们要价太高了。
senses.why: A seller's price is a request for money, so the request sense narrows to money in trade.
senses.whyCN: 卖方的价钱就是在索取钱款，于是「请求」义在交易中窄化为「要价」。

intro.en: Ask is an Old English verb of inquiry that has widened into requests and invitations.
intro.cn: ask 是一个表示询问的古英语动词，后来扩展到请求与邀请。

items.en: ascian meant 'to ask, to inquire'.
items.cn: ascian 意为「问、打听」。

items.en: A northern form ahsian existed beside it.
items.cn: 当时还有一个北方形式 ahsian。

items.en: asken kept the question sense and added requesting.
items.cn: asken 保留询问义，并添上请求义。

items.en: Asking someone to dinner meant inviting.
items.cn: 请人吃饭的说法即表示邀请。

items.en: The price sense settled in trade and advertising.
items.cn: 要价义在交易与广告中固定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group is the ask family; the near-meaning group splits questioning, requesting, and inviting.
note.cn: 形近组是 ask 词族；近义组分别对应询问、请求与邀请。

normalIntro.en: Ask covers a question, a favour, an invitation, and a price.
normalIntro.cn: ask 涵盖提问、请求、邀请与要价。

normal.en: Ask for means to request a thing.
normal.cn: ask for 意为索要某物。

normal.en: Ask someone to do means to request an action.
normal.cn: ask someone to do 意为请某人做某事。

normal.en: Ask after someone means to inquire about health.
normal.cn: ask after someone 意为问候健康。

normal.en: The past tense is asked, not askt.
normal.cn: 过去式是 asked，不是 askt。

normal.en: The vowel differs in British and American speech.
normal.cn: 英式与美式发音的元音不同。

abstract.en: See a mouth opening to form a question.
abstract.cn: 想象一张嘴张开准备提问。

abstract.en: See an open palm waiting for something.
abstract.cn: 想象摊开的手掌等着接东西。

abstract.en: See a price tag held up for approval.
abstract.cn: 想象举起价签让人过目。

examples.en: She asked the assistant where the lift was.
examples.cn: 她问店员电梯在哪里。

examples.en: He asked for a glass of water.
examples.cn: 他要了一杯水。

examples.en: They asked us to dinner on Friday.
examples.cn: 他们请我们周五去吃晚饭。

dict_mnemonic.text: ask 的核心是「开口要一个回应」：要答案就是问，要东西就是求，要人来就是请。

root: 源自古英语 ascian「问、打听」，另有北方形式 ahsian；由询问扩展到请求、邀请，再在交易中固定为要价。

sensesIntro.en: One act of speaking toward another person serves for questions, favours, guests, and prices.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个朝向他人开口的动作，兼用于提问、求助、请客与开价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spoken question held out toward another person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句问话被递到对方面前。

intro.en: A native verb whose derivatives are few and plain.
intro.cn: 这是一个本族动词，派生词少而朴素。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and has no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，没有拉丁词根。

definition_en: in a state of sleep, or without feeling in a part of the body
core_image: 呼吸放慢，眼皮合上不再动
scene: 客厅的灯还亮着，电视在放旧片。The child was asleep before the film ended.
sceneCN: 这里 asleep 是「睡着的」（第 1 个义项：处于睡眠状态）；句意是电影结束前孩子就睡着了。

collocations.zh: 开车时打瞌睡；疏于职守

senses.title: In a state of sleep
senses.definition: sleeping, with the mind and body at rest
senses.definitionCN: 正在睡觉，身心处于休息状态
senses.example: The child was asleep before the film ended.
senses.exampleCN: 电影结束前孩子就睡着了。
senses.why: Asleep is a- 'on' plus sleep: to be on sleep is to be in that state rather than performing the act.
senses.whyCN: asleep 由 a-「在」与 sleep 构成：处在睡眠之中，强调状态而非动作。

senses.title: Without feeling
senses.definition: numb, of a limb that has lost sensation
senses.definitionCN: 肢体失去知觉
senses.example: My foot was asleep after the long bus ride.
senses.exampleCN: 长途汽车坐久了，我的脚麻了。
senses.why: A numb limb feels dead to the world, so the image of sleep shifts from the whole person to one part.
senses.whyCN: 麻木的肢体对外界毫无感觉，于是「睡」的形象从整个人移到某个部位。

intro.en: Asleep is a native compound of on and sleep.
intro.cn: asleep 是 on 与 sleep 构成的本族复合词。

items.en: slæpan meant 'to sleep'.
items.cn: slæpan 意为「睡觉」。

items.en: slæp was the noun 'sleep'.
items.cn: slæp 是名词「睡眠」。

items.en: The phrase on slepe meant 'in sleep'.
items.cn: 短语 on slepe 意为「在睡眠中」。

items.en: The phrase fused into asleep.
items.cn: 这一短语融合为 asleep。

items.en: The numb-limb sense grew from the idea of deadened feeling.
items.cn: 麻木义由「感觉死寂」的观念发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group is the sleep family; the near-meaning group gives words for sleeping and numb.
note.cn: 形近组是 sleep 词族；近义组是表示睡着与麻木的词。

normalIntro.en: Asleep describes the state, not the act.
normalIntro.cn: asleep 描述的是状态，而不是动作。

normal.en: It follows the verb to be or to fall.
normal.cn: 它跟在 be 或 fall 之后。

normal.en: Do not say very asleep; say fast asleep.
normal.cn: 不说 very asleep，而说 fast asleep。

normal.en: A sleeping baby, but a baby asleep.
normal.cn: 作定语用 sleeping，作表语用 asleep。

normal.en: A numb foot is described as asleep.
normal.cn: 脚麻了可以用 asleep 形容。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-SLEEP.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-SLEEP。

abstract.en: See a chest rising and falling slowly.
abstract.cn: 想象胸口缓缓起伏。

abstract.en: See a handshake that cannot feel the hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一只握不出感觉的手。

abstract.en: See a lamp still on over a still face.
abstract.cn: 想象灯还亮着，脸上却毫无动静。

examples.en: The child was asleep before the film ended.
examples.cn: 电影结束前孩子就睡着了。

examples.en: My foot was asleep after the long bus ride.
examples.cn: 长途汽车坐久了，我的脚麻了。

examples.en: She fell asleep with the book still open.
examples.cn: 书还摊着，她就睡着了。

dict_mnemonic.text: a-（在）加 sleep（睡眠）：处在睡眠状态中，就是睡着的；肢体失去感觉也叫「睡着」。

root: 由古英语短语 on slæpe「在睡眠中」融合而成，a- 表示「在」；由整体睡眠状态引申出肢体麻木义。

sensesIntro.en: A whole body at rest and a limb without feeling share the picture of sleep.
sensesIntro.cn: 整个身体休息与某处肢体失去感觉，共用同一个「睡」的形象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: closed eyes and slow breathing.
core.cn: 核心意象：合上的眼与放慢的呼吸。

intro.en: A fused phrase that works only as a predicate adjective.
intro.cn: 这是一个融合的短语，只作表语形容词使用。

latinIntro.en: The root sleep is Germanic; there is no Latin element.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 sleep 属日耳曼语，没有拉丁成分。

definition_en: one part of a situation, the look of something, or the direction a place faces
core_image: 同一件东西从不同角度看，显出不同的面
scene: 报告只写了成本，没提对居民的影响。The report ignores the human aspect of the change.
sceneCN: 这里 aspect 是「方面」（第 1 个义项：整体中的一个侧面）；句意是报告忽略了这一变化涉及人的方面。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：方面的；（语法）体的

senses.title: One side of a matter
senses.definition: a particular part of a larger situation or subject
senses.definitionCN: 较大情况或主题中的一个特定部分
senses.example: The report ignores the human aspect of the change.
senses.exampleCN: 报告忽略了这一变化涉及人的方面。
senses.why: Latin aspicere meant 'to look at'; the aspect is what a matter looks like from one direction.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 aspicere 意为「看」；aspect 就是一件事从某个方向看过去的样子。

senses.title: The look of something
senses.definition: the appearance a thing presents
senses.definitionCN: 事物呈现出来的外貌
senses.example: The house took on a gloomy aspect in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨中这房子显得阴沉。
senses.why: Since aspect is what is seen, it can name the visible face of a place or a face itself.
senses.whyCN: 既然 aspect 是被看见的东西，它就能指一个地方或一张面孔可见的样子。

senses.title: The direction something faces
senses.definition: the way a building or slope faces
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物或坡面所朝的方向
senses.example: A southern aspect keeps the garden warm.
senses.exampleCN: 朝南的朝向让花园保持温暖。
senses.why: The direction from which a place is viewed also decides how much light it receives, hence the compass sense.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方被观看的方向也决定它受多少光，于是产生表示方位的用法。

intro.en: Aspect comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to look at'.
intro.cn: aspect 来自一个意为「看」的拉丁动词。

items.en: specere meant 'to look, to see'.
items.cn: specere 意为「看、看见」。

items.en: ad plus specere meant 'to look toward'.
items.cn: ad 与 specere 结合，意为「朝……看」。

items.en: aspectus meant 'a look, an appearance'.
items.cn: aspectus 意为「目光、外观」。

items.en: English aspect first meant the look of a face or sky.
items.cn: 英语 aspect 最初指面孔或天空的样子。

items.en: The word widened to any side of a question.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到问题的任何一个侧面。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the spect root; the near-meaning group gives feature, side, and view.
note.cn: 形近组保留 spect 词根；近义组给出 feature、side 与 view。

normalIntro.en: An aspect is one face of a many-sided thing.
normalIntro.cn: aspect 就是多面之物的一面。

normal.en: An aspect of is the usual pattern.
normal.cn: an aspect of 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: In grammar, aspect marks how an action unfolds.
normal.cn: 语法里，aspect 表示动作的进行方式。

normal.en: The compas sense survives in estate writing.
normal.cn: 方位义仍见于房产描述文字。

normal.en: The plural is aspects.
normal.cn: 复数是 aspects。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AS-pect.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AS-pect。

abstract.en: See a cube turned to show one face.
abstract.cn: 想象立方体转动，露出一面。

abstract.en: See a window facing south light.
abstract.cn: 想象朝南接光的窗。

abstract.en: See the same event from two balconies.
abstract.cn: 想象从两个阳台看同一件事。

examples.en: The report ignores the human aspect of the change.
examples.cn: 报告忽略了这一变化涉及人的方面。

examples.en: The house took on a gloomy aspect in the rain.
examples.cn: 雨中这房子显得阴沉。

examples.en: A southern aspect keeps the garden warm.
examples.cn: 朝南的朝向让花园保持温暖。

dict_mnemonic.text: a-（向）加 spect（看）：朝某个方向看过去所见的那一面，就是一个方面。

root: 来自拉丁语 aspectus「外观、目光」，源自动词 aspicere「朝……看」，由 ad 与 specere「看」构成；由「所见之面」引申为方面与朝向。

sensesIntro.en: What you see from one side is a face, a look, or a direction.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一侧看见的东西，可以是一面、一种外观，也可以是一个朝向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cube turned so one face catches the light.
core.cn: 核心意象：立方体转动，一面接住光。

intro.en: A Latin noun of looking that English turned toward ideas.
intro.cn: 这是一个拉丁语「观看」名词，英语把它转向了抽象观念。

latinIntro.en: The root specere also gives inspect, respect, and spectator.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 specere 也派生出 inspect、respect 与 spectator。

definition_en: to judge the value or quality of something, or to set a tax on it
core_image: 法官身旁有人翻着卷宗，为每件事标出分量
scene: 保险公司派人来看被水泡过的墙。An engineer came to assess the damage.
sceneCN: 这里 assess 是「评估」（第 1 个义项：判断情况的性质与程度）；句意是工程师来评估损失程度。

pos.zh: 动词：评估；估算；核定（税额）

senses.title: Judge value or quality
senses.definition: to judge or decide the amount, value or quality of something
senses.definitionCN: 判断某事的数量、价值或好坏
senses.example: An engineer came to assess the damage.
senses.exampleCN: 一位工程师来评估损失。
senses.why: Assess comes from Latin assidere 'to sit beside', originally of an assistant sitting next to a judge, so the core act is sitting down to weigh a case.
senses.whyCN: assess 源自拉丁语 assidere「坐在旁边」，原指坐在法官身旁协助断案，核心动作就是坐下来衡量一桩事情。

senses.title: Set a tax or fine
senses.definition: to calculate and set the amount of a tax or fine to be paid
senses.definitionCN: 计算并确定应缴的税额或罚款
senses.example: The city assesses a tax on every rented flat.
senses.exampleCN: 市里对每套出租房征税。
senses.why: The act of weighing value entered the treasury: once a property's worth is judged, a tax can be fixed on it, and that fixing became a sense of its own.
senses.whyCN: 衡量价值的动作进入财政领域：先判定财产值多少，再据此定税，这个「定额」的环节单独成了一个义项。

intro.en: Assess began as a word about sitting beside a judge and ended as a word about weighing value.
intro.cn: assess 起初指坐在法官身旁，最后变成衡量价值的词。

items.en: assidere meant 'to sit beside', used of a judge's assistant.
items.cn: assidere 意为「坐在旁边」，用于说法官的助手。

items.en: assessus was the one who sat beside and helped fix a penalty.
items.cn: assessus 指坐在旁边协助定罚的人。

items.en: assessare meant 'to fix the amount of a tax'.
items.cn: assessare 意为「核定税额」。

items.en: English assessen kept the tax sense, valuing property for payment.
items.cn: 英语 assessen 保留税务义，为征税而估定财产价值。

items.en: The sense widened from tax to any judgement of value or quality.
items.cn: 词义从税务扩大到对任何事物的价值与质量作出判断。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the assess shape; the near-meaning group gives other verbs of judging value.
note.cn: 形近组与 assess 外形相近；近义组是其他表示估值的动词。

normalIntro.en: Think of the assessor who sits beside the judge and writes down a figure.
normalIntro.cn: 想象估税员坐在法官身旁，写下一个数字。

normal.en: The double s belongs to the stem: as-sess, not a-sess.
normal.cn: 词干里是双 s：as-sess，不要写成单 s。

normal.en: It takes a direct object: assess the damage, assess the risk.
normal.cn: 它直接带宾语：评估损失、评估风险。

normal.en: The noun keeps the double s: assessment.
normal.cn: 名词拼作 assessment，中间保留双 s。

normal.en: Use it when a judgement needs evidence, not for a quick guess.
normal.cn: 需要依据作出判断时用它，随口一猜不用它。

normal.en: In tax talk it means to fix a sum, not to collect it.
normal.cn: 在税务语境里指核定金额，而不是收取。

abstract.en: See a hand weighing a folder on a brass scale.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把卷宗放上铜天平称量。

abstract.en: See a stamp pressed onto a property list, fixing a figure.
abstract.cn: 想象印章压在房产清单上，定下一个数目。

abstract.en: See a doctor reading a chart before speaking.
abstract.cn: 想象医生先看完病历再开口。

examples.en: An engineer came to assess the damage.
examples.cn: 一位工程师来评估损失。

examples.en: The city assesses a tax on every rented flat.
examples.cn: 市里对每套出租房征税。

examples.en: Teachers assess students on both writing and speaking.
examples.cn: 老师从写作和口语两方面评估学生。

dict_mnemonic.text: as-（在旁）加 sess（坐）：坐在旁边替人衡量，就是评估；衡量财产以定税，就是核定税额。

root: 源自拉丁语 assidere「坐在旁边」，经中世纪拉丁语 assessare「核定税额」进入英语，由「坐在法官身旁断案」引申为评估，再专指核定税额。

sensesIntro.en: Weighing a situation and fixing a tax are two stages of the same seated judgement.
sensesIntro.cn: 衡量情况与核定税额，是同一个「坐下来判断」的两个阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure written beside a case after it has been weighed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一桩事情称量过后，旁边写下一个数字。

branches.en: the flat was assessed at a high figure
branches.cn: 这套房被估定为一个高数额

intro.en: Assess is built on the Latin verb for sitting, and the same root runs through session and preside.
intro.cn: assess 建立在拉丁语「坐」的动词上，同一词根贯穿 session 与 preside。

latinIntro.en: The root sess or sid, 'to sit', comes from Latin sedere.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 sess 或 sid 意为「坐」，来自拉丁语 sedere。

definition_zh: 评估；评定；评价；教育测评；核定（税额）；评估结果
definition_en: the act of judging the value, quality, or amount of something, a formal judgement, a test of learning, or a tax fixed by authority
core_image: 一叠批改过的作文与一支红笔，旁边写着定好的分数
scene: 学期末的办公桌上摊着一摞作文，红笔在每页的分数栏里落下数字。The assessment of each essay took about ten minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 assessment 是「评估、评定」（第 1 个义项：判断价值或质量的行为）；句意为「每篇作文的评定大约花了十分钟」。画面中有摊开的作文、红笔与分数栏。

pos.zh: 名词：评估；评定；评价；教育测评；核定税额；评估结果

derivatives.zh: assessment 的动词形式，义为「评估；评定；核定」
由 assess 加 -or 构成，义为「评估员；估税员」
由 assess 加 -able 构成，义为「可评估的；可征税的」
由前缀 re- 加 assessment 构成，义为「重新评估」

senses.title: The act of judging value or quality
senses.definition: the act of judging or estimating the value, quality, or seriousness of something
senses.definitionCN: 判断或估算某物的价值、质量或严重程度的行为
senses.example: The assessment of each essay took about ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 每篇作文的评定大约花了十分钟。
senses.why: -ment turns the verb assess into the action itself: the sitting-beside and weighing is now a named event.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 把动词 assess 变成动作本身：那场「坐在旁边称一称」如今成了一个有名字的事件。

senses.title: A test of learning
senses.definition: a formal test or judgement of a pupil's progress, often spread over a course
senses.definitionCN: 对学生学习进展的正式测评，常贯穿整个课程
senses.example: The course uses continuous assessment instead of one final exam.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课采用持续性评价，而不是一次期末考试。
senses.why: If weighing a pupil's work is assess, then the whole system of weighing is an assessment.
senses.whyCN: 如果评一份作业是 assess，那么整套称量的制度就是 assessment。

senses.title: A tax fixed by authority
senses.definition: an official calculation of the tax or fine owed by a person or property
senses.definitionCN: 对个人或财产应缴税款、罚金的官方计算
senses.example: The tax assessment arrived with the winter bill.
senses.exampleCN: 税额核定单随冬季账单一起寄到。
senses.why: This is the oldest official use: an assessor sits beside the property and names the sum.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的官方用法：估税员坐在产业旁边，报出一个数目。

senses.title: The judgement reached
senses.definition: the opinion or rating that results from assessing something
senses.definitionCN: 评估某物之后得出的意见或评级
senses.example: Her assessment was that the plan needed more time.
senses.exampleCN: 她的评价是这个计划还需要更多时间。
senses.why: By shifting from the act to its result, an assessment becomes the verdict someone has reached.
senses.whyCN: 由行为转指结果，assessment 便成了某人得出的结论。

intro.en: Assessment is the noun of assess, and both keep the Latin image of an official sitting beside a property to fix its value.
intro.cn: assessment 是 assess 的名词，两者都保留着「官员坐在产业旁边核定价值」这一拉丁意象。

items.en: The root 「*sed-」 meant 'to sit', and it lies behind many Latin words for sitting and settling.
items.cn: 词根「*sed-」意为「坐」，拉丁语中许多表示坐与安顿的词都由它而来。

items.en: Assidere meant 'to sit beside', from ad- 'to' plus sedere 'to sit'.
items.cn: assidere 意为「坐在旁边」，由 ad-「向」加 sedere「坐」构成。

items.en: An assessor sat beside a magistrate to fix taxes and fines.
items.cn: assessor 坐在长官旁边，协助核定税额与罚金。

items.en: Assesser carried the verb into French with the sense of fixing what is owed.
items.cn: 古法语 assesser 把这个动词带进法语，意思是核定应缴数额。

items.en: English assess began with taxes, and assessment followed as its noun.
items.cn: 英语的 assess 先用于税务，assessment 随后作为它的名词出现。

items.en: Education gave the word a large new field: continuous assessment now weighs pupils, not property.
items.cn: 教育为这个词开辟了大片新领域：持续性评价如今称量的是学生，而非产业。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns close to assessment in form; the near-meaning group gathers evaluations, appraisals and reviews.
note.cn: 形近组收形式上与 assessment 接近的名词；近义组收评估、鉴定与复查。

entries.definition: A person who assesses, especially one who values property for tax.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「评估员、估税员」。

entries.definition: A part cut off from a whole.
A confident statement that something is true.
A careful judgement of value or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 对价值或质量的仔细判断。

entries.definition: A judgement of worth, often of property or performance.
entries.definitionCN: 对价值的评估，常指房产或表现。

entries.definition: An opinion or decision formed after thought.
entries.definitionCN: 经过思考后形成的意见或决定。

entries.definition: An examination of something to judge its state or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 为判断状况或质量而进行的检查。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from marked essays to a school report, a tax notice and a spoken verdict.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子从批改过的作文，走到成绩报告、税单与一句口头结论。

normal.en: Assessment is assess turned into a named event.
normal.cn: assessment 是把 assess 变成一个有名有姓的事件。

normal.en: An assessment of essays: each one is weighed.
normal.cn: 作文评估：每一篇都过一回秤。

normal.en: Continuous assessment: the weighing never stops.
normal.cn: 持续性评价：称量一直没停。

normal.en: A tax assessment: the property is weighed for what it owes.
normal.cn: 税额核定：产业被称一称，看它该缴多少。

normal.en: Her assessment was a verdict in one sentence.
normal.cn: 她的一句评价就是最终结论。

abstract.en: The noun names the act and then the verdict.
abstract.cn: 这个名词先指动作，再指结论。

abstract.en: Tax and school both use the same scale.
abstract.cn: 税务与学校用的是同一架天平。

abstract.en: Every assessment needs a standard to weigh against.
abstract.cn: 任何评估都需要一个可比照的标准。

examples.en: The assessment of each essay took about ten minutes.
examples.cn: 每篇作文的评定大约花了十分钟。

examples.en: The course uses continuous assessment instead of one final exam.
examples.cn: 这门课采用持续性评价，而不是一次期末考试。

examples.en: Her assessment was that the plan needed more time.
examples.cn: 她的评价是这个计划还需要更多时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿塞斯门」——阿塞斯门坐在办公桌前，把每份作业都称一称、打个分：评估

root: assessment 是 assess 加名词后缀 -ment。assess 来自拉丁语 assidere「坐在旁边」，由 ad-「向」与 sedere「坐」构成；assessor 原是坐在长官旁边核定税额的官员。因此 assessment 先指「核定应缴数额」这一官方行为，后泛指判断价值、质量、风险的行为，再指教育中的测评制度，最后由行为转指得出的评价与结论。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses grow from one weighing: the act of judging, a course-wide test of learning, an official tax sum, and the verdict reached.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项从同一次称量长出来：判断的行为、贯穿课程的测评、官方核定的税额，以及最终得出的结论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of marked essays beside a red pen and a column of scores.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠批改过的作文，旁边是一支红笔与一列分数。

branches.en: THE WEIGHING LINE: judging value or quality is the core act.
branches.cn: 称量线：判断价值或质量是核心动作。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL LINE: the weighing becomes a course-long system.
branches.cn: 学校线：称量变成贯穿课程的制度。

branches.en: THE TAX LINE: an official fixes what a property owes.
branches.cn: 税务线：官员定下产业该缴多少。

branches.en: THE VERDICT LINE: the act turns into the opinion reached.
branches.cn: 结论线：动作转成得出的意见。

branches.en: THE REPORT LINE: a written assessment records both the act and the verdict.
branches.cn: 报告线：书面评估同时记录动作与结论。

intro.en: Assessment is assess plus -ment; its family adds -or, -able and the prefix re-.
intro.cn: assessment 是 assess 加 -ment，词族再加 -or、-able 与前缀 re-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root sedere 'to sit' also gave assessor and sedentary, keeping the image of sitting beside.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 sedere「坐」还生出 assessor 与 sedentary，保留着「坐在旁边」的形象。

items.meaning: the act or result of judging
items.example: The assessment was fair to both sides.
items.exampleCN: 这项评估对双方都算公道。

items.example: The school holds two assessments each term.
items.exampleCN: 学校每学期进行两次测评。

items.meaning: to judge or fix a value
items.example: We assess the risk before every flight.
items.exampleCN: 每次飞行前我们都会评估风险。

items.meaning: able to be assessed or taxed
items.example: The gift is not assessable income.
items.exampleCN: 这笔赠与不属于应税收入。

items.example: The city reassessed the flood risk.
items.exampleCN: 城市重新评估了洪水风险。

items.meaning: judging one's own work or tax
items.meaningCN: 自我评估；自行申报纳税
items.example: Self-assessment saves the office a visit.
items.exampleCN: 自行申报省得跑一趟税务局。

latinEntries.meaning: one who sits beside to judge
latinEntries.meaningCN: 坐在旁边协助判断的人
latinEntries.example: The assessor set the fine at ten pounds.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 估税员把罚金定为十英镑。

latinEntries.example: A sedentary life weakens the legs.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 久坐的生活会让腿变弱。

definition_en: to help someone by doing part of the work, or to help make a goal
core_image: 有人站在旁边，伸手扶住摇晃的梯子
scene: 手术室里器械不断递到医生手边。A nurse assisted the surgeon during the operation.
sceneCN: 这里 assist 是「协助」（第 1 个义项：在旁边帮忙）；句意是手术中一名护士协助外科医生。

senses.title: Help by sharing the work
senses.definition: to help someone, especially by doing part of their work
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某人，尤其替他分担一部分工作
senses.example: A nurse assisted the surgeon during the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术中一名护士协助外科医生。
senses.why: Assist comes from Latin assistere, 'to stand by', so the picture is someone standing beside you and lending a hand rather than taking over.
senses.whyCN: assist 源自拉丁语 assistere「站在旁边」，画面是有人站到你身边搭把手，而不是代替你去做。

senses.title: Help make a goal
senses.definition: in sport, to pass or play so that another player scores
senses.definitionCN: 在体育比赛中传球配合，使队友得分
senses.example: He assisted the winning goal in the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一分钟助攻了制胜球。
senses.why: The same image of standing beside and enabling another's success narrows in sport to the pass that lets a teammate score.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「站在旁边促成别人成功」的形象，在球场上收窄为那一脚让队友得分的传球。

intro.en: Assist is built from Latin words for standing, and its oldest picture is standing beside someone.
intro.cn: assist 由拉丁语中表示「站」的词构成，最古老的画面是站到某人身边。

items.en: sistere meant 'to stand, to place'.
items.cn: sistere 意为「站立、放置」。

items.en: assistere meant 'to take one's stand beside'.
items.cn: assistere 意为「站到旁边」。

items.en: assister meant 'to be present and give help'.
items.cn: assister 意为「在场并给予帮助」。

items.en: English assisten meant 'to help or support'.
items.cn: 英语 assisten 意为「帮助、支援」。

items.en: Sport added the sense of setting up a goal.
items.cn: 体育领域增出「为进球做球」的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sist root; the near-meaning group gives other verbs for helping.
note.cn: 形近组共享 sist 词根；近义组是其他表示帮助的动词。

entries.definition: to stand firmly on a claim
to make things easier for someone

normalIntro.en: To assist is to stand beside, not to stand in front.
normalIntro.cn: assist 是站到旁边，而不是站到前面代替。

normal.en: It usually takes a person as object: assist the surgeon.
normal.cn: 它通常以人作宾语：协助外科医生。

normal.en: The preposition is with for a task and in for a process.
normal.cn: 接任务用 with，接过程用 in。

normal.en: The double s comes from as- plus sist.
normal.cn: 双 s 来自 as- 与 sist 的结合。

normal.en: It is more formal than help.
normal.cn: 它比 help 正式。

normal.en: In football an assist is a pass, not a goal.
normal.cn: 足球里的助攻是一次传球，不是进球。

abstract.en: See one hand steadying a ladder while another climbs.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扶稳梯子，另一人往上爬。

abstract.en: See a nurse's hand arriving before it is asked for.
abstract.cn: 想象护士的手在开口之前就递到了。

abstract.en: See a pass rolled into the path of a runner.
abstract.cn: 想象一脚球滚到队友跑动的线路上。

examples.en: A nurse assisted the surgeon during the operation.
examples.cn: 手术中一名护士协助外科医生。

examples.en: He assisted the winning goal in the last minute.
examples.cn: 他在最后一分钟助攻了制胜球。

examples.en: Two students assisted with the survey.
examples.cn: 两名学生协助做了这项调查。

dict_mnemonic.text: as-（在旁边）加 sist（站）：站在旁边搭把手，就是协助；球场上帮队友得分的那一脚，就是助攻。

root: 源自拉丁语 assistere「站到旁边」，由 ad-「向」与 sistere「站」构成；由「在场支援」引申为帮助，现代又衍生出体育中的助攻义。

sensesIntro.en: Standing beside someone explains both lending a hand and setting up a score.
sensesIntro.cn: 「站在旁边」既能解释搭把手，也能解释为队友做球。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching in from the side.
core.cn: 核心意象：从侧面伸过来的一只手。

intro.en: Assist belongs to the sist family, where the root means standing.
intro.cn: assist 属于 sist 词族，这个词根表示「站」。

latinIntro.en: Latin sistere, 'to stand', also gives insist, resist and persist.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sistere「站」还产生了 insist、resist 与 persist。

items.meaning: to stand firm on a claim

definition_en: help given to someone, especially official or financial help
core_image: 一只手从旁边伸过来，托住快要倒下的东西
scene: 老人提着两袋菜站在楼梯口。A neighbour offered assistance with the bags.
sceneCN: 这里 assistance 是「帮助」（第 1 个义项：给予的援手）；句意是邻居主动帮忙提袋子。

senses.title: Help that is given
senses.definition: help that someone gives to another person
senses.definitionCN: 一个人给予另一个人的援手
senses.example: A neighbour offered assistance with the bags.
senses.exampleCN: 一位邻居主动帮忙提袋子。
senses.why: Assistance is assist plus -ance, a suffix naming a state or an act, so it treats the help as something handed over rather than as one person's deed.
senses.whyCN: assistance 是 assist 加 -ance，这个后缀表示状态或行为，因此它把帮助看作被递过来的一份援手，而不是某个人的一次动作。

senses.title: Official or financial aid
senses.definition: money or support provided by an institution or government
senses.definitionCN: 由机构或政府提供的钱款与支援
senses.example: The family applied for government assistance.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人申请了政府补助。
senses.why: When the hand that helps belongs to an office or a fund rather than a neighbour, the word settles into the sense of formal aid paid out by an institution.
senses.whyCN: 当伸出的手来自机构或基金而不是邻居时，这个词就固定指由机构发放的正式援助与补助。

intro.en: Assistance is the abstract noun of assist, made with a suffix of state and action.
intro.cn: assistance 是 assist 的抽象名词，由表示状态与行为的名词后缀构成。

items.en: sistere meant 'to stand'.
items.cn: sistere 意为「站」。

items.en: assistere meant 'to stand beside'.
items.cn: assistere 意为「站在旁边」。

items.en: assister meant 'to be present and help'.
items.cn: assister 意为「在场帮忙」。

items.en: English formed assistance from assist on the French pattern.
items.cn: 英语仿照法语构词法，由 assist 造出 assistance。

items.en: The word widened to official and financial aid.
items.cn: 词义扩大到官方援助与资金补助。

note.en: The look-alike group is the assist family; the near-meaning group names help and support.
note.cn: 形近组是 assist 词族；近义组是表示帮助与支援的词。

entries.definition: the act of making things easier

normalIntro.en: Assistance is the help itself, not the person giving it.
normalIntro.cn: assistance 指帮助本身，不指给帮助的人。

normal.en: It is uncountable: some assistance, not an assistance.
normal.cn: 它不可数：说 some assistance，不说 an assistance。

normal.en: The fixed phrases are with the assistance of and be of assistance.
normal.cn: 固定说法是 with the assistance of 与 be of assistance。

normal.en: For the person, use assistant; for the act, use assistance.
normal.cn: 指人用 assistant，指行为用 assistance。

normal.en: It sounds more formal than help.
normal.cn: 它比 help 正式。

normal.en: Financial assistance is a common official phrase.
normal.cn: financial assistance 是常见的官方说法。

abstract.en: See a hand catching a box before it falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在箱子落地前托住它。

abstract.en: See a form signed so that money can be released.
abstract.cn: 想象一份表格签好，钱才能发放。

abstract.en: See a stranger holding a door without being asked.
abstract.cn: 想象陌生人没被请求就替你扶住门。

examples.en: A neighbour offered assistance with the bags.
examples.cn: 一位邻居主动帮忙提袋子。

examples.en: The family applied for government assistance.
examples.cn: 这家人申请了政府补助。

examples.en: She finished the report with the assistance of two colleagues.
examples.cn: 在两位同事的帮助下，她完成了报告。

dict_mnemonic.text: assist（协助）加 -ance（行为、状态）：被给出来的援助。邻里的援手是帮助，机构发放的钱款是补助。

root: 由 assist 加 -ance 构成；assist 源自拉丁语 assistere「站在旁边」，因此 assistance 指被提供的援手，现代常指机构发放的正式援助与补助。

sensesIntro.en: A hand from a neighbour and funds from an office are both help that is handed over.
sensesIntro.cn: 邻居伸的手与机构拨的钱，都是被递过来的一份帮助。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steadying hand arriving from the side.
core.cn: 核心意象：从侧面伸来的一只扶持的手。

branches.en: with the assistance of a friend

intro.en: The -ance ending marks a noun of state, as in resistance and insistence.
intro.cn: 结尾 -ance 表示状态名词，resist 与 insist 的名词也这样构成。

latinIntro.en: The base sistere, 'to stand', is Latin, and it spreads across many English verbs.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 sistere「站」来自拉丁语，衍生出许多英语动词。

definition_en: a person who helps someone more senior, or a junior rank
core_image: 站在主事者侧后方，随时接过手里的活
scene: 诊所里，年轻人先登记病人的信息。The assistant booked the next patient in.
sceneCN: 这里 assistant 是「助手」（第 1 个义项：协助他人工作的人）；句意是助手为下一位病人登记。

senses.title: Person who helps
senses.definition: a person employed to help someone with their work
senses.definitionCN: 受雇帮助某人完成工作的人
senses.example: The assistant booked the next patient in.
senses.exampleCN: 助手为下一位病人做了登记。
senses.why: The Latin ending -ant marks the doer, so assistant is literally 'the one standing beside', the person who takes part of the work off another's hands.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语后缀 -ant 标记动作的执行者，所以 assistant 字面就是「站在旁边的那个人」，替别人分担一部分工作。

senses.title: Junior rank before a title
senses.definition: used before a job title to show a rank below it
senses.definitionCN: 放在职位名称前，表示低一级的职位
senses.example: She was promoted to assistant manager last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 去年春天她升为副经理。
senses.why: A helper who stands beside a senior post naturally gave a name to the rank just under it, so the noun came to modify titles directly.
senses.whyCN: 站在主管职位旁边的帮手，很自然成了紧挨其下的那一级职务的名称，于是这个名词直接修饰职位头衔。

intro.en: Assistant turns the verb assist into a person by way of a Latin ending for the doer.
intro.cn: assistant 借拉丁语表示「做事者」的后缀，把动词 assist 变成指人的名词。

items.en: sistere meant 'to stand'.
items.cn: sistere 意为「站」。

items.en: assistere meant 'to stand beside'.
items.cn: assistere 意为「站在旁边」。

items.en: assistens was 'the one standing by'.
items.cn: assistens 指「站在旁边的人」。

items.en: English assistant named a helper in a household or office.
items.cn: 英语 assistant 指家庭或事务所里帮忙的人。

items.en: Shop assistant and assistant manager fixed the modern uses.
items.cn: 店员与副经理这两种说法固定了现代用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the assist stem; the near-meaning group names helpers and deputies.
note.cn: 形近组共享 assist 词干；近义组是表示帮手与副职的词。

normalIntro.en: An assistant is defined by position: beside and slightly behind.
normalIntro.cn: 助手的位置很明确：在旁边，稍靠后。

normal.en: It is a countable person noun: an assistant, two assistants.
normal.cn: 它是可数的人称名词：一名助手、两名助手。

normal.en: In British shops a shop assistant serves customers.
normal.cn: 英式英语里 shop assistant 指售货员。

normal.en: As a title modifier it means deputy: assistant manager.
normal.cn: 作头衔修饰语时表示副职：副经理。

normal.en: The ending -ant marks the person, as in servant.
normal.cn: 结尾 -ant 标记执行者，如 servant。

normal.en: Stress falls on the second syllable: as-SIS-tant.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

abstract.en: See a second chair set slightly behind a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象办公桌后方稍偏处摆着第二把椅子。

abstract.en: See a clipboard passed over without a word.
abstract.cn: 想象一块记录板被默默递过去。

abstract.en: See a nameplate that begins with the word assistant.
abstract.cn: 想象一块以「助理」开头的小名牌。

examples.en: The assistant booked the next patient in.

dict_mnemonic.text: assist（协助）加 -ant（做某事的人）：站在旁边帮忙的人就是助手；放在职位前，就成了副职。

root: 源自拉丁语 assistere「站在旁边」，由 assist 加表示执行者的 -ant 构成；本指在场帮忙的人，后也用作职位前的「助理、副」这一级别。

sensesIntro.en: The person beside the desk and the rank just below the title come from the same position.
sensesIntro.cn: 桌旁的那个人与头衔下的一级，来自同一个「在旁边」的位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second chair behind and beside the main desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：主桌后侧的第二把椅子。

intro.en: The -ant ending turns an action into the person who performs it.
intro.cn: 结尾 -ant 把动作变成执行该动作的人。

latinIntro.en: Latin sistere, 'to stand', is the base of a large family of English words.

definition_zh: 联想；把……联系起来；交往；同事
definition_en: to connect things in the mind, to spend time with people, or a person you work with
core_image: 两条原本分开的线在脑中打了一个结
scene: 一闻到消毒水味，她就想起医院。That smell is associated with the hospital.
sceneCN: 这里 associate 是「联想到」（第 1 个义项：把两件事在脑中连起来）；句意是那股气味让人联想到医院。

senses.title: Connect in the mind
senses.definition: to connect one thing with another in your mind
senses.definitionCN: 在头脑中把一件事与另一件事连起来
senses.example: That smell is associated with the hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 那股气味让人联想到医院。
senses.why: Associate comes from Latin associare, 'to join as a companion', built on socius 'companion', so the core act is pairing two things so that one calls up the other.
senses.whyCN: associate 源自拉丁语 associare「使结为同伴」，词基 socius 意为同伴，所以核心动作是把两样东西配成伴，见到一个就想起另一个。

senses.title: Spend time with people
senses.definition: to spend time with a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 与某人或某群体经常相处
senses.example: He associates with artists and writers.
senses.exampleCN: 他常与画家和作家来往。
senses.why: When the companionship is between people rather than ideas, the same joining becomes the plain act of keeping company with a group.
senses.whyCN: 当「结伴」发生在人与人之间而不是概念之间时，同一个连接动作就落成了与某群人来往这一日常含义。

senses.title: Work partner
senses.definition: a person you work or do business with
senses.definitionCN: 一起工作或做生意的人
senses.example: She met a business associate at the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 她在机场见了一位生意伙伴。
senses.why: The noun form names the companion who has been joined to you by work, so it covers colleagues and business partners without implying friendship.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式指因工作而与你结伴的人，因此既能指同事，也能指生意伙伴，并不暗示私人交情。

intro.en: Associate is built on the Latin word for a companion, and its senses all keep the idea of joining.
intro.cn: associate 建立在拉丁语「同伴」一词上，各义项都保留「结成伴」的意思。

items.en: socius meant 'companion or ally'.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴、盟友」。

items.en: associare meant 'to join with as a companion'.
items.cn: associare 意为「结为同伴」。

items.en: associer meant 'to unite or combine'.
items.cn: associer 意为「联合、结合」。

items.en: English associate covered both company and mental linking.
items.cn: 英语 associate 兼指结伴与脑中的联系。

items.en: The noun sense 'colleague' settled in business use.
items.cn: 名词「同事」义在商业语境中固定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the soci root; the near-meaning group gives verbs of linking and mingling.
note.cn: 形近组共享 soci 词根；近义组是表示连接与交往的动词。

normal.en: The verb ends in -ate and is stressed on the second syllable.
normal.cn: 动词以 -ate 结尾，重音在第二音节。

normal.en: The noun is stressed differently and means a partner.
normal.cn: 名词重音不同，指伙伴。

normal.en: The pattern is associate A with B.

normal.en: Be associated with is the passive form seen in reports.
normal.cn: 报告中常见被动形式 be associated with。

normal.en: The soci part also appears in social and society.
normal.cn: soci 这一部分也出现在 social 与 society 中。

abstract.en: See a name card exchanged across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象桌面上交换的一张名片。

abstract.en: See a bell that rings whenever a certain face appears.
abstract.cn: 想象某张脸一出现，铃就响。

examples.cn: 那股气味让人联想到医院。

examples.en: He associates with artists and writers.
examples.cn: 他常与画家和作家来往。

examples.cn: 她在机场见了一位生意伙伴。

dict_mnemonic.text: as-（向）加 soci（同伴）加 -ate：把两样东西结成伴，就是在脑中建立联系；人与人结成伴，就是交往；结成伴的人就是同事。

root: 源自拉丁语 socius「同伴」与 associare「结为同伴」，经古法语 associer 进入英语；由「结成伴」引申为联想、联系与交往，名词指结伴工作的人。

sensesIntro.en: Ideas, people and colleagues are all joined as companions, only the kind of partner changes.
sensesIntro.cn: 概念、交往对象与同事都是被结成伴的东西，变的只是同伴的种类。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two threads knotted together.
core.cn: 核心意象：两根线被系在一起。

branches.en: associate a name with a face

intro.en: The root soci, 'companion', joins a large family of social words.
intro.cn: 词根 soci 意为「同伴」，串起一大族与社会有关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin socius is the source of social, society and sociable.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 socius 是 social、society 与 sociable 的来源。

items.exampleCN: 把气味与地点联系起来

definition_en: an organized group, or a connection between things
core_image: 一群人围着同一张桌子坐下
scene: 街角的老楼门口挂起一块新牌子。The residents formed an association to save the building.
sceneCN: 这里 association 是「协会」（第 1 个义项：为共同目的组成的团体）；句意是居民们成立协会来保住这栋楼。

senses.title: Organized group
senses.definition: an organized group of people with a shared purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为共同目的组织起来的一群人
senses.example: The residents formed an association to save the building.
senses.exampleCN: 居民们成立协会来保住这栋楼。
senses.why: Association is associate plus -ion, so a verb meaning 'to join as companions' becomes the body of companions who have joined, that is, an organized group.
senses.whyCN: association 是 associate 加 -ion，把「结为同伴」的动词变成结成伴的那一群人，也就是有组织的团体。

senses.title: Connection or mental link
senses.definition: a connection between two things, including one made in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 两件事之间的关联，也包括脑中的联想
senses.example: The study found an association between sleep and memory.
senses.exampleCN: 研究发现了睡眠与记忆之间的关联。
senses.why: The same joining, once it is between facts or ideas rather than people, becomes a link that can be measured or merely felt in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「结伴」如果发生在事实或观念之间而不是人之间，就成了可以被测量或只在脑中感到的关联。

intro.en: Association is the noun of joining, used both for groups of people and for links between things.
intro.cn: association 是表示「结合」的名词，既指人的团体，也指事物之间的关联。

items.en: socius meant 'companion'.
items.cn: socius 意为「同伴」。

items.en: associare meant 'to join together'.
items.cn: associare 意为「结合在一起」。

items.en: Old French associer kept the sense of uniting.
items.cn: 古法语 associer 保留「联合」之义。

items.en: Association named a guild or a body of people.
items.cn: association 指行会或一群有组织的人。

items.en: Psychology gave the word its sense of a mental link.
items.cn: 心理学赋予它「脑中联想」的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the associ stem; the near-meaning group names groups and links.
note.cn: 形近组共享 associ 词干；近义组是表示团体与关联的词。

normalIntro.en: An association can be a room full of members or a thread between two facts.
normalIntro.cn: association 可以是一屋子会员，也可以是两个事实之间的一根线。

normal.en: The ending -tion marks the noun built on associate.
normal.cn: 结尾 -tion 标记由 associate 构成的名词。

normal.en: In association with means working together with another body.
normal.cn: in association with 指与另一机构合作。

normal.en: In research writing it often means a statistical link.
normal.cn: 在研究写作里它常指统计上的关联。

normal.en: Stress the fourth syllable: as-so-ci-A-tion.
normal.cn: 重音在第四个音节。

normal.en: Do not drop the second i in spelling.
normal.cn: 拼写时不要漏掉第二个 i。

abstract.en: See a long table with name cards around it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，四周摆着名牌。

abstract.en: See a thin line drawn between two words on a page.
abstract.cn: 想象书页上两个词之间画了一条细线。

abstract.en: See a key ring holding many keys of one building.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋楼的许多钥匙串在一个环上。

examples.en: The residents formed an association to save the building.
examples.cn: 居民们成立协会来保住这栋楼。

examples.en: The study found an association between sleep and memory.
examples.cn: 研究发现了睡眠与记忆之间的关联。

examples.en: She works in association with a local charity.
examples.cn: 她与一家本地慈善机构合作。

dict_mnemonic.text: associate（结伴）加 -ion：结成伴的一群人是协会；结成伴的两件事是联系，脑中的联系就是联想。

root: 由 associate 加 -ion 构成；associate 源自拉丁语 socius「同伴」，因此 association 既指因共同目的结成的人群，也指事物之间乃至脑中的关联。

sensesIntro.en: People joining and ideas joining share one noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 人结成伴与观念结成伴，共用一个名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: separate names written on one membership list.
core.cn: 核心意象：各自的名字写在同一张会员名册上。

branches.en: an association between sleep and memory

intro.en: The -ion ending turns the verb of joining into the thing or state that results.
intro.cn: 结尾 -ion 把表示结合的动词变成结合后的事物或状态。

latinIntro.en: The root soci, 'companion', also underlies society and sociology.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 soci「同伴」也是 society 与 sociology 的来源。

definition_en: to suppose without proof, to take on a duty, or to begin to have a quality
core_image: 一件外套被人直接披到自己身上
scene: 会议没核对数据就开始讨论。Everyone assumed the figures were correct.
sceneCN: 这里 assume 是「假定」（第 1 个义项：没有证据就先当作成立）；句意是大家都假定这些数字是对的。

senses.title: Suppose without proof
senses.definition: to believe that something is true without proof
senses.definitionCN: 在没有证据时先认定某事成立
senses.example: Everyone assumed the figures were correct.
senses.exampleCN: 大家都假定这些数字是对的。
senses.why: Assume comes from Latin assumere, 'to take up', so taking a claim up as your own is to accept it before it has been proved.
senses.whyCN: assume 源自拉丁语 assumere「拿起来」，把一种说法拿过来当作自己的，就是在被证实之前先接受它。

senses.title: Take on a duty
senses.definition: to take on responsibility, power or an office
senses.definitionCN: 接过责任、权力或职位
senses.example: She assumed control of the company in June.
senses.exampleCN: 她在六月接管了公司。
senses.why: The literal Latin sense of taking something onto oneself survives here: power or duty is picked up and carried by the new holder.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语「取到自己身上」的本义在这个义项里保留下来：权力或责任被新的承担者接过去扛起来。

senses.title: Begin to have a quality
senses.definition: to begin to have a particular quality or appearance
senses.definitionCN: 开始带有某种性质或外表
senses.example: The sky assumed a deep red before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨前天空呈现出深红色。
senses.why: Putting on an appearance is the same gesture as putting on a coat, so the word can describe a look that something takes on.
senses.whyCN: 把某种外表披到自己身上，与披上一件外套是同一个动作，因此这个词也能说某物呈现出某种样子。

intro.en: Assume is a Latin verb of taking, and every sense keeps something of that gesture.
intro.cn: assume 是拉丁语中表示「拿取」的动词，各个义项都保留着这个动作的影子。

items.en: sumere meant 'to take or take up'.
items.cn: sumere 意为「拿、取」。

items.en: assumere meant 'to take to oneself'.
items.cn: assumere 意为「取到自己身上」。

items.en: assumptus was the taking up of a burden or a claim.
items.cn: assumptus 指接过负担或接受某种主张。

items.en: assumer meant 'to take on or claim'.
items.cn: assumer 意为「承担、主张」。

items.en: English added the sense of taking on an appearance.
items.cn: 英语又增出「呈现出某种外表」的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sume root; the near-meaning group gives other verbs of supposing and taking on.
note.cn: 形近组共享 sume 词根；近义组是表示假定与承担的动词。

entries.definition: to think something is probably true
to agree to do a task
to take as true on likelihood

normalIntro.en: Assume is always a taking: a claim, a duty or a look.
normalIntro.cn: assume 始终是一个「拿」的动作：拿走一种说法、一份职责或一副外表。

normal.en: The pattern assume that is common in argument.
normal.cn: 论证中常见 assume that 结构。

normal.en: Assume responsibility is the formal way to say take the blame or duty.
normal.cn: assume responsibility 是承担责任的正式说法。

normal.en: The past participle assumed can mean pretended.
normal.cn: 过去分词 assumed 可表示「假装的」。

normal.en: Do not confuse assume with presume, which is based on likelihood.
normal.cn: 不要与 presume 混淆，后者带有「有理由推定」的意味。

normal.en: The s sounds like a soft z in the middle.
normal.cn: 中间的 s 读作近似 z 的浊音。

abstract.en: See a coat lifted from a hook and put on without asking.
abstract.cn: 想象一件外套被从钩子上取下，不问自穿。

abstract.en: See a signature on a line that says responsibility.
abstract.cn: 想象在写着「责任」的那一栏签下名字。

abstract.en: See a face turning the colour of the sky before rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸变成雨前天空的颜色。

examples.en: Everyone assumed the figures were correct.
examples.cn: 大家都假定这些数字是对的。

examples.en: She assumed control of the company in June.
examples.cn: 她在六月接管了公司。

examples.en: The sky assumed a deep red before the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨前天空呈现出深红色。

dict_mnemonic.text: as-（向）加 sume（拿）：把一种说法拿过来当作自己的，是假定；把权力与责任拿过来，是承担；把一副样子披上身，是呈现。

root: 源自拉丁语 assumere「取到自己身上」，由 ad-「向」与 sumere「拿」构成；由「拿过来」引申为未经证实便接受，再引申为承担职责与呈现外表。

sensesIntro.en: Taking a claim, a duty or a look are three objects of the same grasping verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 拿走一种说法、一份职责或一副外表，是同一个「取」的动作面对三种对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something lifted and placed on oneself.
core.cn: 核心意象：一样东西被拿起并放到自己身上。

intro.en: The root sume, 'to take', runs through consume, resume and presume.
intro.cn: 词根 sume 意为「拿」，贯穿 consume、resume 与 presume。

latinIntro.en: Latin sumere is the base, and its compounds spread across daily English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sumere 是词基，它的复合词遍布日常英语。

definition_en: something accepted as true without proof, or the act of taking on a duty
core_image: 一块没有验过的地基被当作稳固
scene: 报告开头先列了三条前提。The plan rests on the assumption that prices stay flat.
sceneCN: 这里 assumption 是「假定」（第 1 个义项：未经验证就被接受的前提）；句意是计划建立在物价不变这一假定上。

senses.title: Thing taken as true
senses.definition: something you accept as true without proof
senses.definitionCN: 未经证明就被当作成立的前提
senses.example: The plan rests on the assumption that prices stay flat.
senses.exampleCN: 计划建立在物价不变这一假定上。
senses.why: Assumption is assume plus -tion, turning the act of taking a claim up into the claim itself, the thing a plan leans on before proof arrives.
senses.whyCN: assumption 是 assume 加 -tion，把「拿过来接受」的动作变成被接受的那条内容，也就是计划在证据到来前所倚靠的前提。

senses.title: Act of taking on
senses.definition: the act of taking on power, duty or an office
senses.definitionCN: 接过权力、职责或职位的行为
senses.example: The assumption of office takes place in May.
senses.exampleCN: 就职仪式在五月举行。
senses.why: The old Latin sense of taking something onto oneself survives as a formal noun for entering an office or taking up a duty.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语「取到自己身上」的旧义保留下来，成为正式说法，指就任职位或承担职责。

intro.en: Assumption is the noun of taking up, whether a belief or an office.
intro.cn: assumption 是「拿起、接过」的名词，接过的可以是一种看法，也可以是一个职位。

items.en: sumere meant 'to take'.
items.cn: sumere 意为「拿」。

items.en: assumere meant 'to take to oneself'.
items.cn: assumere 意为「取到自己身上」。

items.en: assumptio meant 'a taking up'.
items.cn: assumptio 意为「拿起、接过」。

items.en: Old French assumer kept both the logical and official senses.
items.cn: 古法语 assumer 兼有逻辑与职务两方面的含义。

items.en: English assumption fixed the sense of an unproved premise.
items.cn: 英语把 assumption 固定为「未经证明的前提」。

note.en: The look-alike group is the sume family; the near-meaning group names premises and guesses.
note.cn: 形近组是 sume 词族；近义组是表示前提与推测的词。

a statement an argument starts from

normalIntro.en: An assumption is a floor nobody has tested before building on it.
normalIntro.cn: assumption 是一块没验过就被踩上去的地板。

normal.en: The phrase on the assumption that introduces the unproved point.
normal.cn: 短语 on the assumption that 引出那个未经验证的判断。

normal.en: In academic writing assumptions are usually stated and then tested.
normal.cn: 学术写作里通常先点明假设，再加以检验。

normal.en: The second sense is formal and appears with office or power.
normal.cn: 第二个义项较正式，常与职位或权力连用。

normal.en: The ending is -tion, so the noun refers to a thing or an act.
normal.cn: 结尾是 -tion，因此名词指事物或行为。

normal.en: Do not write an assumption of that for the everyday sense.
normal.cn: 日常「假定」义不用 an assumption of that 这种结构。

abstract.en: See a house built on a slab nobody checked.
abstract.cn: 想象房子盖在一块没人检查过的板上。

abstract.en: See a question mark drawn over a number in a report.
abstract.cn: 想象报告里的数字上被画了问号。

abstract.en: See a hand receiving a seal of office.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手接过任职印章。

examples.en: The plan rests on the assumption that prices stay flat.
examples.cn: 计划建立在物价不变这一假定上。

examples.en: The assumption of office takes place in May.
