examples.en: Her argument begins with a false assumption.
examples.cn: 她的论证从一个错误的假设开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: assume（假定、承担）加 -tion：被拿过来当作前提的那条内容是假设；把职位接过来这件事本身，是就任。

root: 源自拉丁语 assumptio「拿起、接过」，由 assumere「取到自己身上」构成；指未经证明便接受的前提，也指正式接任职位与承担责任。

sensesIntro.en: A belief picked up without proof and an office picked up in ceremony are both things taken.
sensesIntro.cn: 未经证明就接受的看法，与在仪式上接过的职位，都是被「拿起」的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a floor laid down before anyone tests it.
core.cn: 核心意象：还没人验过就铺好的地板。

intro.en: The noun keeps the Latin sense of taking, with -tion marking the result.
intro.cn: 这个名词保留拉丁语「拿取」之义，-tion 标记结果。

latinIntro.en: Sumere, 'to take', gives a whole set of English nouns in -tion.
latinIntro.cn: sumere「拿」产生了一整组以 -tion 结尾的英语名词。

definition_en: to surprise someone very much, or to shock by something hard to believe
core_image: 一声雷在头顶炸开，人愣在原地
scene: 魔术师从帽子里变出一只活鸽子。The trick astonished the children.
sceneCN: 这里 astonish 是「使惊讶」（第 1 个义项：因意外而让人愣住）；句意是这个戏法让孩子们大为惊讶。

pos.zh: 动词：使大为惊讶；使震惊

senses.title: Surprise greatly
senses.definition: to surprise someone very much by something unexpected
senses.definitionCN: 因出乎意料之事而让人极为惊讶
senses.example: The trick astonished the children.
senses.exampleCN: 这个戏法让孩子们大为惊讶。
senses.why: Astonish goes back to Latin extonare, 'to strike with thunder', so the original picture is a person stunned by a clap overhead.
senses.whyCN: astonish 可追溯到拉丁语 extonare「雷击」，最初的画面就是人被头顶的一声雷震得愣住。

senses.title: Shock by something hard to believe
senses.definition: to shock someone with news or an event that seems unbelievable
senses.definitionCN: 用难以相信的消息或事件使人震惊
senses.example: The scale of the damage astonished the inspectors.
senses.exampleCN: 损失的规模让检查人员震惊。
senses.why: When the thunderbolt is bad news rather than a trick, the same stunned stillness reads as shock, which is why the word also covers disbelief at something grave.
senses.whyCN: 当那道雷不是戏法而是坏消息时，同样的僵住就成了一种震惊，所以这个词也能表示对严重事件的难以置信。

intro.en: Astonish is a thunder word: its ancestors describe being struck by lightning.
intro.cn: astonish 是个打雷的词，它的祖辈词描述被雷电击中。

items.en: tonare meant 'to thunder'.
items.cn: tonare 意为「打雷」。

items.en: extonare meant 'to strike with thunder'.
items.cn: extonare 意为「以雷击打」。

items.en: estoner meant 'to stun or amaze'.
items.cn: estoner 意为「震住、使惊愕」。

items.en: astonen meant 'to stun the mind'.
items.cn: astonen 意为「使心神震住」。

items.en: The spelling settled as astonish, with the thunder forgotten.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 astonish，打雷的画面渐渐被遗忘。

note.en: The look-alike group is the astonish family; the near-meaning group gives other verbs of surprise.
note.cn: 形近组是 astonish 词族；近义组是其他表示惊讶的动词。

entries.definition: to upset with a sudden event

normalIntro.en: Think of a thunderclap that leaves a person standing still.
normalIntro.cn: 想象一声雷把人劈在原地不动。

normal.en: The subject is the startling thing, the object is the person.
normal.cn: 主语是令人吃惊的事物，宾语是人。

normal.en: The adjective astonishing describes the thing, astonished the person.
normal.cn: astonishing 形容事物，astonished 形容人。

normal.en: The noun is astonishment.
normal.cn: 名词是 astonishment。

normal.en: It is stronger than surprise.
normal.cn: 它比 surprise 程度更重。

normal.en: The middle syllable is stressed: as-TON-ish.
normal.cn: 重音在中间音节。

abstract.en: See a dove pulled from an empty hat.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鸽子从空帽子里被拎出来。

abstract.en: See a listener frozen with a cup halfway to the mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象听的人僵住，杯子停在半空。

abstract.en: See a flash and then a room gone silent.
abstract.cn: 想象一道闪光之后，整个房间静下来。

examples.en: The trick astonished the children.
examples.cn: 这个戏法让孩子们大为惊讶。

examples.en: The scale of the damage astonished the inspectors.
examples.cn: 损失的规模让检查人员震惊。

examples.en: She astonished us all by finishing first.
examples.cn: 她第一个完成，让我们都很吃惊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 词源里藏着「雷」：拉丁语 extonare 是被雷击中。人被雷劈中般僵住，就是大为惊讶；遇到难以相信的坏消息，就是震惊。

root: 源自拉丁语 extonare「以雷击打」，由 ex- 加强语气与 tonare「打雷」构成，经古法语 estoner 进入英语；由「被雷震住」引申为大为惊讶与震惊。

sensesIntro.en: A wonderful trick and a terrible scale of damage can both freeze a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 精彩的戏法与骇人的损失规模，都能让人僵在原地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thunderclap directly overhead.
core.cn: 核心意象：头顶炸开的一声雷。

intro.en: The word carries a hidden thunder root, ton, visible also in detonate.
intro.cn: 这个词藏着表示「雷」的词根 ton，在 detonate 里也能看到。

latinIntro.en: Latin tonare, 'to thunder', and its compounds entered English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tonare「打雷」及其复合词经法语进入英语。

definition_zh: 宇航员；航天员；航天飞行乘组成员
definition_en: a person who is trained to travel and work in a spacecraft
core_image: 一个穿着白色宇航服的人被绑进座椅，身后是火箭尾焰和漆黑天空
scene: 电视直播里主持人激动地说：The astronaut floated into the space station and waved at the camera.
sceneCN: 这里指「乘航天器进入太空的人」（第 1 个义项：接受训练乘航天器上太空的人）；句意为宇航员飘进空间站，对着镜头挥手。

pos.zh: 宇航员；航天员；乘航天器进入太空的人

derivatives.zh: 天文学家（共享 astro- 词根，但研究而非飞行）

senses.title: A trained space traveler
senses.titleCN: 受训乘航天器进入太空的人
senses.definition: a person trained by a space program to travel and work aboard a spacecraft
senses.definitionCN: 由航天计划训练、乘航天器进入太空并在其上工作的人
senses.example: The astronaut spent six months aboard the space station.
senses.exampleCN: 这位宇航员在空间站上待了六个月。
senses.why: The word literally means 'star sailor': someone who sails among the stars, so the core image is a person riding a craft through space.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面意思是「星际水手」：在群星间航行的人，所以核心意象是乘飞行器穿越太空的人。

senses.title: A crew member of a space mission
senses.definition: one of the people assigned to fly a particular space mission, whether pilot, scientist or engineer
senses.definitionCN: 被指派执行某次航天飞行任务的人员，无论担任飞行员、科学家还是工程师
senses.example: Each astronaut on the mission had a different job during launch.
senses.exampleCN: 任务中每位宇航员在发射时承担不同的职责。
senses.why: Spacecraft carry crews like ships carry sailors, so astronaut extends to every member of that crew.
senses.whyCN: 航天器像船载水手一样载着乘组，所以 astronaut 扩展到乘组的每一位成员。

senses.title: A national space program title
senses.definition: the English term for space travelers of the US and international programs, contrasted with cosmonaut and taikonaut
senses.definitionCN: 美国及国际计划中航天员的英语称谓，与俄语 cosmonaut、中文 taikonaut 相对
senses.example: An American astronaut and a Russian cosmonaut shared the same capsule.
senses.exampleCN: 一位美国宇航员和一位俄罗斯宇航员共用同一个返回舱。
senses.why: Different space agencies coined their own words from the same Greek roots, so astronaut names one tradition among several.
senses.whyCN: 各国航天机构用同一批希腊词根造了自己的词，astronaut 只是其中一种传统的称呼。

senses.title: A job or career in spaceflight
senses.definition: the profession of flying in space, requiring years of training in engineering, science and survival
senses.definitionCN: 上太空执行飞行任务的职业，需要在工程、科学和生存训练上投入多年
senses.example: She dreamed of becoming an astronaut since primary school.
senses.exampleCN: 她从小学起就梦想成为宇航员。
senses.why: Because training is long and selective, astronaut also names the career itself, like pilot or sailor.
senses.whyCN: 由于训练漫长且选拔严格，astronaut 也像 pilot、sailor 一样指这份职业本身。

senses.title: Figurative use for a space-like experience
senses.titleCN: 比喻用法：仿佛置身太空的人
senses.definition: informally, someone in a situation that feels weightless, isolated or otherworldly
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法，指处于失重、隔绝或仿佛在另一个世界的人
senses.example: With all the noise cancelling on, I felt like an astronaut in my own bubble.
senses.exampleCN: 开着降噪耳机，我感觉自己像置身太空泡泡里的宇航员。
senses.why: The image of a lone figure floating in a white suit is so vivid that people borrow it for any isolated, floating experience.
senses.whyCN: 白色宇航服里孤独漂浮的形象太鲜明，人们借它形容任何隔绝、漂浮般的处境。

senses.title: Historic and pioneer astronauts
senses.definition: people remembered as the first or most famous space travelers, such as Yuri Gagarin or Neil Armstrong
senses.definitionCN: 作为最早或最著名航天者被记住的人，如加加林、阿姆斯特朗
senses.example: Schoolchildren learn the name of the first astronaut who orbited the Earth.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们都要学习第一位绕地球飞行的宇航员的名字。
senses.why: Because spaceflight is young, each milestone astronaut is a named hero in history books.
senses.whyCN: 航天历史很短，每个里程碑式的宇航员都成了史册上有名有姓的英雄。

senses.title: Astronaut in training or candidates
senses.definition: applicants and trainees who have been selected for a space program but have not yet flown
senses.definitionCN: 已被航天计划选中但尚未上天的候选人和受训者
senses.example: The new class of astronaut candidates begins underwater training next month.
senses.exampleCN: 新一届宇航员候选人下月开始水下训练。
senses.why: Selection is so famous that even people who have never left Earth are already called astronauts in the media.
senses.whyCN: 选拔过程太出名，媒体把还没离开地球的受训者就已经称作宇航员。

senses.title: Everyday and childhood usage
senses.definition: used loosely by children or in play for anyone in a space costume or dreaming of space
senses.definitionCN: 孩子游戏或口语中，泛指穿太空服、向往太空的任何人
senses.example: The toddler in a puffy snowsuit waddled across the room like a little astronaut.
senses.exampleCN: 穿着蓬松雪地服的幼儿像小宇航员一样摇摇摆摆地穿过房间。
senses.why: The costume defines the image, so anything bulky and white invites the nickname astronaut.
senses.whyCN: 服装本身定义了形象，任何白色臃肿的装束都会让人联想到宇航员。

intro.en: astronaut is a modern coinage from Greek astro- (star) and naut- (sailor), literally 'star sailor', modeled on words like aeronaut.
intro.cn: astronaut 是现代造词，来自希腊语 astro-（星）和 naut-（水手），字面义为「星际水手」，仿照 aeronaut 一类词构成。

items.en: Greek astron means 'star' and nautes means 'sailor'; neither formed a classical compound astronaut.
items.cn: 希腊语 astron 意为「星」，nautes 意为「水手」；古希腊语中并没有 astronaut 这样的复合词。

items.en: In the 1920s to 1930s, writers coined astronaut on the model of aeronaut, a balloon traveler of the 18th and 19th centuries.
items.cn: 二十世纪二三十年代，作家们仿照十八九世纪的热气球旅行者 aeronaut，造出了 astronaut 一词。

items.en: Early English uses referred to fictional or imagined space travelers before any real spaceflight existed.
items.cn: 在真实航天出现之前，英语里的 astronaut 最早指小说和想象中的太空旅行者。

items.en: After Gagarin's flight in 1961 and the US Mercury program, astronaut became the official title for American space travelers.
items.cn: 1961 年加加林升空及美国水星计划之后，astronaut 成为美国航天员的正式称谓。

items.en: The Soviet program used cosmonaut (kosmos + nautes) and China later used taikonaut, all built on the same sailor image.
items.cn: 苏联计划用 cosmonaut（宇宙 + 水手），中国后来用 taikonaut（太空 + 水手），都基于同一「航行」意象。

items.en: Today astronaut is the general English word for any professional space traveler, whatever their nationality.
items.cn: 今天 astronaut 是英语中对职业航天员的通称，不问国籍。

note.en: Group one collects astro- words that look or build alike; group two collects near-meaning space traveler terms.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或同用 astro- 词根的词；第二组是语义相近的太空旅行者称谓。

entries.definition: A scientist who studies the stars; shares astro- but studies from Earth rather than flying.
entries.definitionCN: 研究星辰的科学家；共享 astro- 词根，但在地面研究而非上天飞行。

entries.definition: The science of celestial objects; the field an astronaut may fly for but is not itself a person.
entries.definitionCN: 研究天体的学科；宇航员可能为之飞行，但它本身不是人。

entries.definition: One who reads horoscopes; looks close to astronomer but is not a science profession.
entries.definitionCN: 看星盘占卜的人；与 astronomer 拼写相近，但并非科学职业。

entries.definition: The Russian and Soviet term for a space traveler, built on kosmos instead of astron.
entries.definitionCN: 俄苏航天员的称谓，用 kosmos 而非 astron 构词。

entries.definition: The English word for Chinese space travelers, from taikong (space) plus naut.
entries.definitionCN: 中国航天员的英文称谓，来自「太空」加 naut。

entries.definition: Flies aircraft within the atmosphere; an astronaut pilots spacecraft beyond it.
entries.definitionCN: 在大气层内驾驶飞机；宇航员在大气层外驾驶航天器。

normalIntro.en: Remember astronaut as a sailor of the stars: astro- star + naut sailor.
normalIntro.cn: 把 astronaut 记成「星际水手」：astro- 星 + naut 水手。

normal.en: astro- means star, as in astronomy; naut means sailor, as in nautical.
normal.cn: astro- 表示星（如 astronomy）；naut 表示水手（如 nautical 航海的）。

normal.en: cosmonaut and taikonaut share the same -naut tail; only the first part changes by country.
normal.cn: cosmonaut、taikonaut 共用 -naut 尾，只有前半随国家不同。

normal.en: An astronaut trains for years before riding a rocket.
normal.cn: 宇航员上天前要训练好几年。

normal.en: aeronaut (balloon sailor) was the model for astronaut.
normal.cn: aeronaut（气球水手）是 astronaut 的构词蓝本。

normal.en: Think of a white spacesuit floating outside the space station.
normal.cn: 想象空间站外漂浮的一袭白色宇航服。

abstract.en: A tiny white figure drifting above a blue marble that holds everyone you know.
abstract.cn: 小小的白色身影，漂浮在容纳你所有熟人的蓝色圆球之上。

abstract.en: The silence of a helmet: your own breath is the loudest sound.
abstract.cn: 头盔里的寂静：自己的呼吸是最响的声音。

abstract.en: A rope between you and the ship — the only thread home.
abstract.cn: 你和飞船之间的一根系绳——回家唯一的线。

examples.en: The astronaut answered questions from students while floating in zero gravity.
examples.cn: 宇航员在失重漂浮中回答了学生们的问题。

examples.en: Only the healthiest candidates are chosen to become astronauts.
examples.cn: 只有最健康的候选人才能被选为宇航员。

examples.en: Astronauts must exercise daily to keep their muscles strong in orbit.
examples.cn: 宇航员在轨道上必须每天锻炼以保持肌肉力量。

dict_mnemonic.text: astro-（星）+ naut（水手）= 星际水手 = 宇航员

root: 希腊语 astron（星）+ nautes（水手）→ 现代仿 aeronaut 造词 astronaut。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses grow from one image, a person sailing among the stars: the trained traveler, the mission crew, national titles, the career, figurative use, historic pioneers, trainees and playful usage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由「星际航行的人」这一意象展开：受训的旅行者、任务乘组、各国称谓、职业、比喻用法、历史先驱、受训者、童趣用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white-suited sailor floating in black space, tethered to a small ship.
core.cn: 核心意象：白色宇航服的水手漂浮在漆黑太空里，系着一艘小飞船。

branches.en: SPACEFLIGHT: the trained person and their role on a mission crew.
branches.cn: 航天：受训上太空的人及其在任务乘组中的角色。

branches.en: NAMING AND CAREER: national titles like cosmonaut, and spaceflight as a profession.
branches.cn: 称谓与职业：cosmonaut 等各国称谓，以及航天飞行这门职业。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE AND PLAYFUL: anyone who feels space-like or dresses the part.
branches.cn: 比喻与童趣：任何感觉像在太空或穿上太空装的人。

branches.en: HISTORY: the pioneer astronauts remembered by name.
branches.cn: 历史：被记住名字的先驱宇航员。

branches.en: TRAINING: candidates selected but not yet flown.
branches.cn: 训练：已入选但尚未上天的候选人。

intro.en: astronaut is built on Greek astro- (star) and -naut (sailor); the -naut tail also appears in aeronaut, cosmonaut and aquanaut.
intro.cn: astronaut 由希腊语 astro-（星）和 -naut（水手）构成；-naut 尾还出现在 aeronaut、cosmonaut、aquanaut 中。

latinIntro.en: astro- comes from Greek astron; -naut from Greek nautes. Latin passed both shapes into modern scientific coinages.
latinIntro.cn: astro- 来自希腊 astron；-naut 来自希腊 nautes。这两个词形经由现代科学造词沿用至今。

items.meaning: law of the stars; the science

definition_en: a scientist who studies the universe, stars, planets and other celestial bodies
core_image: 一个戴着眼镜、头发花白的老头站在大型望远镜前，抬头望天
scene: 纪录片里解说员说：Edwin Hubble, the astronomer after whom the great telescope was named, proved the universe is expanding.
sceneCN: 这里指「职业是研究天体的科学家」（第1个义项：专业天文学家）；句意为哈勃望远镜命名的那位天文学家证明了宇宙在膨胀。

senses.title: Professional working in the field
senses.definition: a scientist with advanced training in astronomy, employed by observatories, universities or space agencies
senses.definitionCN: 受过高等天文学训练，被天文台、大学或航天机构雇佣的科学家
senses.example: The astronomer stayed up all night collecting data on a rare comet.
senses.exampleCN: 那位天文学家熬夜收集一颗罕见彗星的数据。
senses.why: Like other -er professions, astronomer names the person who does astronomy.
senses.whyCN: 和其他 -er 职业一样，astronomer 就是做 astronomy 的人。

senses.title: Amateur astronomer
senses.definition: a person who observes the sky as a hobby, often with modest equipment but serious enthusiasm
senses.definitionCN: 以观星为爱好的人，设备可能不高级但热情很高
senses.example: An amateur astronomer in Australia spotted a new asteroid before any professional.
senses.exampleCN: 一位澳大利亚业余天文学家比任何职业的都早发现了一颗新小行星。
senses.why: Amateur astronomers can out-professionals when the sky is dark and the target is faint.
senses.whyCN: 业余天文学家能超过职业的，特别是在天空漆黑、目标又暗的时候。

senses.title: Observational vs theoretical
senses.definition: subspecialties: observational astronomers collect data; theoretical astronomers build models
senses.definitionCN: 子专业：观测天文学家收集数据，理论天文学家建立模型
senses.example: She is an observational astronomer who specialises in measuring exoplanet sizes.
senses.exampleCN: 她是专门测量系外行星大小的观测天文学家。
senses.why: Astronomy has the classic split between those who gather evidence and those who explain it.
senses.whyCN: 天文学有经典的分工：收集证据的人和解释证据的人。

senses.title: Historic astronomers
senses.definition: people across cultures who studied the sky before modern science, including Copernicus, Galileo, Kepler, Tycho Brahe
senses.definitionCN: 现代科学之前研究天空的跨文化人物，如哥白尼、伽利略、开普勒、第谷
senses.example: Ancient Arab astronomers gave us most of the star names we still use today.
senses.exampleCN: 古代阿拉伯天文学家给了我们今天仍在使用的大部分星名。
senses.why: Historic astronomers are part of the long tradition that modern astronomy builds on.
senses.whyCN: 历史天文学家是现代天文学所依赖的悠久传统的一部分。

senses.title: Astronomer vs astrophysicist
senses.titleCN: 天文学家 vs 天体物理学家
senses.definition: the boundaries blur; astrophysicists study the physics of celestial objects, astronomers can work in observation or theory broadly
senses.definitionCN: 边界模糊：天体物理学家研究天体物理；天文学家可广泛做观测或理论
senses.example: Many astronomers today are also astrophysicists — the overlap is large.
senses.exampleCN: 今天许多天文学家也是天体物理学家——重叠很大。
senses.why: Both -ist professions share the astron- root, but astrophysicists explicitly study the 'physics' part.
senses.whyCN: 两种 -ist 职业共享 astron- 词根，但 astrophysicist 明确研究 physics 那部分。

senses.title: Astronomer as public scientist
senses.titleCN: 作为公共科学家的天文学家
senses.definition: many astronomers are active science communicators, appearing in documentaries and public talks
senses.definitionCN: 许多天文学家是活跃的科学传播者，出现在纪录片和公共演讲里
senses.example: The astronomer is a regular on late-night science shows.
senses.exampleCN: 这位天文学家是深夜科学节目的常客。
senses.why: Astronomy has broad public appeal — everyone looks up — so astronomers are often the face of science.
senses.whyCN: 天文学有广泛公众吸引力——人人抬头看——所以天文学家常成为科学的脸面。

senses.title: Astronomer at a research facility
senses.titleCN: 科研机构里的天文学家
senses.definition: a staff member of an observatory, space agency or research institute, handling data across projects
senses.definitionCN: 天文台、航天机构或研究所的职员，处理跨项目的数据
senses.example: The observatory employs 12 astronomers to run its flagship telescope.
senses.exampleCN: 这座天文台雇了 12 位天文学家运营它的旗舰望远镜。
senses.why: Big science requires teams, so astronomers work as staff rather than as lone geniuses.
senses.whyCN: 大科学需要团队，所以天文学家是作为职员工作，不是独行天才。

senses.title: Children / dreamers using the word
senses.definition: used informally for anyone fascinated by the sky, not just qualified scientists
senses.definitionCN: 非正式地指任何对天空着迷的人，不只合格科学家
senses.example: As a child I wanted to be an astronomer; now I just look up from the balcony.
senses.exampleCN: 小时候我想当天文学家；现在就从阳台上抬头看看。
senses.why: The word carries wonder, so it's used by dreamers as well as by specialists.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带着浪漫感，所以梦想家和专业人士都用。

intro.en: astronomer adds the English -er agent suffix to astronomy, which itself comes from Greek astron (star) + nomos (law).
intro.cn: astronomer 在 astronomy 上加英语 -er 施事后缀；astronomy 本身来自希腊 astron（星）+ nomos（法）。

items.en: Greek astronomos meant 'one versed in the laws of stars'.
items.cn: 希腊语 astronomos 意为「精通星辰之法的人」。

items.en: Latin astronomus was borrowed directly, meaning 'an astronomer'.
items.cn: 拉丁语直接借入 astronomus，意为「天文学家」。

items.en: Middle English astronomer (14th century) came via Old French astronomier.
items.cn: 中古英语 astronomer（14 世纪）经古法语 astronomier 而来。

items.en: The spelling settled to astronomer, matching astronom- + -er.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 astronomer，对齐 astronom- + -er。

items.en: As astronomy split into subfields, astronomer kept its broad sense while astrophysicist and cosmologist became narrower terms.
items.cn: 当 astronomy 分成子学科时，astronomer 保持广义，而 astrophysicist 和 cosmologist 变得更窄。

items.en: Professional, amateur, historic and popular senses all remain active.
items.cn: 职业、业余、历史、大众的义项今天都仍在使用。

note.en: Group one shares the astron- root with -er / -ist professions; group two are other celestial professionals.
note.cn: 第一组共享 astron- 词根的 -er / -ist 职业；第二组是其他天体领域的专业人士。

entries.definition: General term for someone who studies the sky.
Someone who studies the physics of celestial bodies; subset of astronomer.
entries.definitionCN: 研究天体物理的人；astronomer 的子集。

entries.definition: Astronomer who studies the origin and structure of the whole universe.
entries.definitionCN: 研究整个宇宙起源和结构的天文学家。

entries.definition: Studies life in the universe; not strictly an astronomer.
entries.definitionCN: 研究宇宙中的生命；严格说不算 astronomer。

entries.definition: Flies spacecraft; not a scientist, though many have astronomy backgrounds.
entries.definitionCN: 驾驶航天器的；不是科学家，虽然很多有天文背景。

entries.definition: Uses celestial positions for divination; not a scientist.
entries.definitionCN: 用天体位置占卜；不是科学家。

entries.definition: Bigger category including astronomers, planetary scientists, etc.
entries.definitionCN: 更大的类别，包括天文学家、行星科学家等。

entries.definition: Often an astronomer by training who manages the facility.
entries.definitionCN: 通常是训练有素的天文学家，同时管理天文台。

normalIntro.en: An astronomer is someone who does astronomy.
normalIntro.cn: An astronomer 就是做 astronomy 的人。

normal.en: astronomy + -er = astronomer, just like teacher = teach + -er.
normal.cn: astronomy + -er = astronomer，就像 teacher = teach + -er。

normal.en: Astronomers use telescopes; astrologers use horoscopes.
normal.cn: Astronomers 用望远镜；astrologers 用星盘。

normal.en: Amateur astronomers find comets too — you don't need a PhD.
normal.cn: 业余天文学家也能发现彗星——不一定要博士。

normal.en: Edwin Hubble is the astronomer after whom the telescope is named.
normal.cn: Edwin Hubble 就是哈勃望远镜名字的那位 astronomer。

normal.en: The astronomer stays up all night because the sky is darkest then.
normal.cn: 天文学家熬夜因为那时天空最黑。

abstract.en: A single person in the dark, looking up through glass at light that left a star before the Earth was born.
abstract.cn: 黑暗中的一个人，透过玻璃看着早在地球诞生前就离开恒星的光。

abstract.en: A notebook full of numbers, a red headlamp, cold coffee at 3am.
abstract.cn: 一本写满数字的笔记本、红色头灯、凌晨三点的冷咖啡。

abstract.en: Tiny, alone, and looking upward out of sheer habit.
abstract.cn: 微小、孤独、纯粹出于习惯地向上看。

examples.en: The astronomer's paper on black hole imaging won the biggest prize in physics that year.
examples.cn: 这位天文学家关于黑洞成像的论文那年拿了物理领域最大的奖。

examples.en: My cousin is an amateur astronomer who drives to the desert every new moon.
examples.cn: 我表弟是业余天文学家，每个新月都开车去沙漠。

examples.en: Astronomers from 20 nations collaborated to build the Event Horizon Telescope.
examples.cn: 20 个国家的天文学家合作建了事件视界望远镜。

dict_mnemonic.text: astronomy（天文学）+ -er（做...的人）= 天文学家

root: 希腊语 astron（星）+ nomos（法则）→ astronomy → 加 -er 指「做…的人」→ astronomer。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses describe who astronomers are: professional, amateur, observational, theoretical, historic, boundary-vs-astrophysicist, public communicators, and dreamers.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项讲 astronomer 是谁：职业的、业余的、观测的、理论的、历史上的、与天体物理学家的边界、公共传播者、梦想家。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lone figure at a telescope eyepiece, lit only by a faint red lamp and the stars overhead.
core.cn: 核心意象：目镜前一个孤独的身影，只有微弱红灯和头顶的星光照着。

branches.cn: 边界 / 科普 / 梦想

intro.en: astronomer is astronomy + -er; the -er suffix turns a science name into the person who practises it.
intro.cn: astronomer 就是 astronomy + -er；-er 后缀把一门科学变成做它的人。

latinIntro.en: The astron- root is Greek; -er is English but has Latin cognate -or (as in actor).
latinIntro.cn: astron- 来自希腊；-er 是英语但有拉丁同源 -or（如 actor）。

definition_en: the scientific study of the universe, stars, planets and other celestial bodies
core_image: 一张从地球轨道向外看去的银河全景图，星点密密麻麻
scene: 开学第一节课老师说：Astronomy asks what the universe is made of, how it began, and where it's going.
sceneCN: 这里指「研究宇宙和天体的科学」（第1个义项：科学学科）；句意为天文学追问宇宙由什么构成、如何起源、去往何处。

senses.title: The scientific discipline itself
senses.titleCN: 作为学科本身的天文学
senses.definition: one of the oldest natural sciences, studying everything outside Earth's atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 最古老的自然科学之一，研究地球大气层以外的一切
senses.example: Astronomy has reshaped our picture of the universe in the last century.
senses.exampleCN: 过去一百年里天文学重塑了我们对宇宙的认识。
senses.why: The Greek roots astron (star) + nomos (law) make this the 'law of stars'.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 astron（星）+ nomos（法）让它成为「星辰之法」。

senses.title: Observational astronomy
senses.definition: the branch that gathers data with telescopes, cameras and detectors from the ground or space
senses.definitionCN: 用望远镜、相机和探测器从地面或太空收集数据的分支
senses.example: Observational astronomy got a new eye when the Hubble telescope launched in 1990.
senses.exampleCN: 1990 年哈勃升空给观测天文学添了一只新眼。
senses.why: Observational astronomy is the empirical side, gathering evidence that theorists use.
senses.whyCN: 观测天文学是经验的一面，收集理论家使用的证据。

senses.title: Theoretical astronomy
senses.definition: the branch that builds models to explain what observations reveal
senses.definitionCN: 建立模型解释观测结果的分支
senses.example: Theoretical astronomy predicts where black holes should lie in galaxy centres.
senses.exampleCN: 理论天文学预言黑洞应该在星系中心哪里。
senses.why: Theory gives meaning to observations, turning data into understanding.
senses.whyCN: 理论给观测赋予意义，把数据变成理解。

senses.title: Astronomy history and pre-scientific
senses.titleCN: 前科学的天文观测（历史上）
senses.definition: the ancient practice of tracking skies for calendars, religion or navigation, before the scientific method
senses.definitionCN: 科学方法出现之前，为历算、宗教或导航追踪天象的古老实践
senses.example: Maya astronomy predicted eclipses with remarkable accuracy without telescopes.
senses.exampleCN: 玛雅天文学不用望远镜就以惊人准确度预测了日食月食。
senses.why: Early astronomy blended with astrology, religion and agriculture.
senses.whyCN: 早期天文学与占星、宗教、农业混在一起。

senses.title: Popular astronomy / stargazing
senses.definition: the hobby or public outreach of observing the sky with small telescopes or the naked eye
senses.definitionCN: 用小望远镜或肉眼观星的爱好或科普活动
senses.example: The park hosts free astronomy nights every month for the public.
senses.exampleCN: 公园每月给公众办免费天文之夜。
senses.why: Popular astronomy shares the sky with non-scientists, keeping wonder alive.
senses.whyCN: 科普天文把星空分享给非科学家，让好奇心延续。

senses.title: Subfields: planetary, stellar, galactic
senses.definition: astronomy splits into subfields by object studied: planets, stars, galaxies, the universe as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 按研究对象划分的子学科：行星、恒星、星系、宇宙整体
senses.example: She chose galactic astronomy, studying how the Milky Way formed.
senses.exampleCN: 她选了星系天文学，研究银河系如何形成。
senses.why: Each subfield brings its own tools and questions, but all belong under the same root.
senses.whyCN: 每个子学科有自己的工具和问题，但都在同一词根之下。

senses.title: Astrology vs astronomy
senses.definition: astronomy is the scientific study; astrology uses celestial positions to predict human affairs and is not a science
senses.definitionCN: astronomy 是科学研究；占星用天体位置预言人类事务，不是科学
senses.example: Most universities offer astronomy, none offer astrology as a science.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数大学教 astronomy，没有哪所大学把占星作为科学开设。
senses.why: The -logy ending in astrology sounds scientific but does not mean it uses the scientific method.
senses.whyCN: astrology 里的 -logy 听起来科学但不代表它用科学方法。

senses.title: Influencing other sciences
senses.definition: astronomy overlaps with physics, chemistry, geology, biology and information science
senses.definitionCN: astronomy 与物理、化学、地质、生物、信息科学有交叉
senses.example: Discoveries in astronomy often drive new inventions in sensing and computing.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学的发现常常推动传感和计算的新发明。
senses.why: The universe is the largest laboratory; everything physical here is also physical 'out there'.
senses.whyCN: 宇宙是最大的实验室；这里一切物理事物在「外面」也是物理的。

intro.en: astronomy comes from Greek: astron 'star' + nomos 'law, custom' → 'the law of stars'; it arrived in Latin as astronomia and entered English around the 13th century.
intro.cn: astronomy 来自希腊语：astron「星」+ nomos「法」→「星辰之法」；经拉丁语 astronomia，13 世纪进入英语。

items.en: Aristotle used astronomia to mean the study of celestial motions; nomos meant 'the law that governs'.
items.cn: 亚里士多德用 astronomia 指对天体运动的研究；nomos 意为「支配之法」。

items.en: Latin borrowed astronomia directly from Greek, keeping both the word and the meaning.
items.cn: 拉丁语直接从希腊语借入 astronomia，词和意思都不变。

items.en: Middle English astronomie (13th century) was the standard spelling, borrowed through Old French astronomie.
items.cn: 中古英语 astronomie（13 世纪）是标准拼写，经古法语 astronomie 借入。

items.en: Spelling shifted to astronomy by the 16th century, matching the Greek -nomy suffix pattern.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪拼写变成 astronomy，对齐希腊 -nomy 后缀形式。

items.en: Copernicus and Kepler redefined astronomy in the 16th and 17th centuries as mathematical physics of the heavens.
items.cn: 哥白尼和开普勒在 16-17 世纪把 astronomy 重新定义为天上的数学物理。

items.en: Today astronomy spans from subatomic particles to the structure of the cosmos.
items.cn: 今天 astronomy 从亚原子粒子延伸到宇宙结构。

note.en: Group one holds astronomy-derived words; group two holds related 'sky science' and related -nomy / -logy terms.
note.cn: 第一组是 astronomy 派生的词；第二组是相关的「天空科学」和相近的 -nomy / -logy 术语。

entries.definition: A person who works in astronomy.
Of astronomy; informally, huge in size.
entries.definitionCN: 天文学的；口语里表示「极大的」。

entries.definition: Physics applied to astronomical objects; technically a subfield.
entries.definitionCN: 用物理研究天体；严格说是 astronomy 的子学科。

entries.definition: The study of life in the universe; also called exobiology.
entries.definitionCN: 研究宇宙中的生命；也叫 exobiology。

entries.definition: Not a science; uses celestial positions to interpret human affairs.
entries.definitionCN: 非科学；用天体位置解读人类事务。

entries.definition: The part of astronomy that studies the origin and structure of the whole universe.
entries.definitionCN: 研究整个宇宙起源和结构的 astronomy 分支。

entries.definition: The specific study of how the universe began; narrower than cosmology.
entries.definitionCN: 专门研究宇宙如何起源；范围比 cosmology 窄。

entries.definition: Describing and mapping the universe rather than modelling its physics.
entries.definitionCN: 描述和绘制宇宙，而非建模其物理。

normalIntro.en: astron- = star, -nomy = law → astronomy = the law of stars.
normalIntro.cn: astron- = 星，-nomy = 法 → astronomy = 星辰之法。

normal.en: astron (Greek for star) + nomos (Greek for law) = astronomy.
normal.cn: astron（希腊语「星」）+ nomos（希腊语「法」）= astronomy。

normal.en: An astronomer follows the laws of stars.
normal.cn: 天文学家追随星辰之法。

normal.en: People once called astronomy 'the science of the stars'.
normal.cn: 人们曾经把 astronomy 叫「星辰的科学」。

normal.en: Astronomy uses telescopes; astrology uses horoscopes.
normal.cn: Astronomy 用望远镜；占星用星盘。

normal.en: Kepler wrote the laws of planetary motion — laws of stars.
normal.cn: 开普勒写了行星运动定律——星辰之法。

abstract.en: A clear night, the Milky Way overhead, a telescope pointing somewhere deep.
abstract.cn: 晴朗的夜，头顶银河，望远镜指向深处某处。

abstract.en: A thousand-year quest to figure out where we are and why.
abstract.cn: 一场绵延千年的追问：我们在哪、为什么。

abstract.en: Something ancient, vast, and always pointing up.
abstract.cn: 一种古老、浩瀚、永远向上指的东西。

examples.en: Radio astronomy began in the 1930s when engineers accidentally picked up cosmic radio noise.
examples.cn: 射电天文学始于 1930 年代，工程师无意中接收到宇宙射电噪声。

examples.en: Astronomy is a team science; modern observations involve telescopes on every continent and in space.
examples.cn: astronomy 是团队科学；现代观测涉及每个大陆和太空的望远镜。

examples.en: Her PhD combined astronomy with statistics to hunt for exoplanets.
examples.cn: 她的博士结合了天文学和统计来寻找系外行星。

dict_mnemonic.text: astron-（星）+ -nomy（法）= 星辰之法 = 天文学

root: astron（希腊语，星）+ nomos（法）→ astronomia → astronomy。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses map the many ways we study the sky: observing, theorising, history, popular enthusiasm, subfields, distinguishing from astrology, and influence on other sciences.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项覆盖我们研究天空的种种方式：观测、理论、历史、业余爱好、子学科、与占星区分、对其他科学的影响。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a telescope pointed at a dark sky, pulling faint stars into bright focus.
core.cn: 核心意象：指向暗空的望远镜，把暗淡的星辰拉成清晰的焦点。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE AND OBSERVATION: the field itself, plus the work of watching and measuring the sky.
branches.cn: 学科与观测：这门学科本身，以及观测测量天空的工作。

branches.en: THEORETICAL: the branch that builds models and predictions.
branches.cn: 理论：负责建立模型与预言的分支。

branches.en: HISTORICAL: pre-scientific sky watching and its records.
branches.cn: 历史：前科学时期的天象观测及其记录。

branches.en: POPULAR / OUTREACH: amateur stargazing and public explanation.
branches.cn: 科普 / 业余：业余观星与面向公众的解释。

branches.en: CLASSIFICATION / BOUNDARIES / INFLUENCE: subfields, the line against astrology, and effects on other sciences.
branches.cn: 分类 / 边界 / 影响：子学科、与占星的界线，以及对其他学科的影响。

intro.en: astronomy is built from Greek astron 'star' plus the Greek suffix -nomy 'law, system of rules'; many astronomy words share astron-.
intro.cn: astronomy 由希腊 astron「星」加希腊后缀 -nomy「法、规则体系」构成；许多 astronomy 相关词都共享 astron-。

latinIntro.en: astron is purely Greek, not Latin; the Latin 'star' is stella, which gives stellar.
latinIntro.cn: astron 纯粹来自希腊，不是拉丁语；拉丁语的「星」是 stella，给出 stellar。

items.meaning: study of the laws of stars
one who navigates among the stars

definition_zh: 在（某处）；在（某时）；以（某种速度、程度）
definition_en: used to show a point in place or time, or a rate and level
core_image: 手指点在地图上的一个点
scene: 两个人约在车站门口见面。We met at the station gate.
sceneCN: 这里 at 是「在」（第 1 个义项：指一个具体的点）；句意是我们在车站门口见面。

senses.title: A point in place
senses.definition: used to show an exact point or place
senses.definitionCN: 表示一个确切的地点或位置点
senses.example: We met at the station gate.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站门口见面。
senses.why: At goes back to Old English æt, a word for touching a point, which is why it marks a spot rather than the inside of a place.
senses.whyCN: at 可追溯到古英语 æt，本指触到某一点，所以它标的是一个位置点，而不是某地的内部。

senses.title: A point in time
senses.definition: used to show an exact moment
senses.definitionCN: 表示一个确切的时刻
senses.example: The train leaves at six.
senses.exampleCN: 火车六点开。
senses.why: The same pointing gesture moves onto the time line: a clock reading is treated as one dot on the day.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「点一下」的动作移到时间轴上：一个钟点被看成一天里的一个点。

senses.title: A rate or level
senses.definition: used to show a speed, price, level or manner
senses.definitionCN: 表示速度、价格、程度或方式
senses.example: He drove at sixty miles an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 他以每小时六十英里的速度开车。
senses.why: Fixing a value at one point on a scale is the same act of pointing, so the word also marks rates, prices and states.
senses.whyCN: 把数值定在刻度上的某一点，也是同一个「指」的动作，因此这个词也用来标速度、价格与状态。

intro.en: At is one of the oldest English prepositions, and its meaning has stayed close to 'touching a point'.
intro.cn: at 是英语最古老的介词之一，含义一直贴近「触到一点」。

items.en: æt meant 'at, near, in'.
items.cn: æt 意为「在、靠近、于」。

items.en: Cognates in related languages also meant 'at'.
items.cn: 同语系语言中的同源词也表示「在」。

items.en: At spread to time expressions such as at night.
items.cn: at 扩展到 at night 这类时间说法。

items.en: Fixed phrases with rates and prices became common.
items.cn: 表示速度与价格的固定说法开始常见。

items.en: At remains a core preposition of point and level.
items.cn: at 至今仍是表示「点」与「刻度」的核心介词。

note.en: The look-alike group is short words easily confused with at; the near-meaning group is the other place prepositions.
note.cn: 形近组是容易与 at 混淆的短词；近义组是其他地点介词。

normalIntro.en: At marks a dot, not a box: a point on a map, a clock or a scale.
normalIntro.cn: at 标的是一个点，不是一个盒子：地图上的点、钟点或刻度上的点。

normal.en: Use at for a point, in for an enclosed space, on for a surface.
normal.cn: 点用 at，封闭空间用 in，表面用 on。

normal.en: Clock times take at: at six, at noon.
normal.cn: 钟点前用 at：六点、正午。

normal.en: Rates and prices take at: at speed, at ten dollars.
normal.cn: 速度与价格前用 at。

normal.en: The weak form sounds like a short unstressed syllable.
normal.cn: 弱读时是一个很轻的短音。

normal.en: Do not use at with a period such as in the morning.
normal.cn: 表示上午这类时段时不用 at，而用 in。

abstract.en: See a fingertip pressed on one spot of a map.
abstract.cn: 想象指尖按在地图的某一个点上。

abstract.en: See a clock hand stopped at one number.
abstract.cn: 想象指针停在一个数字上。

abstract.en: See a needle resting on one mark of a dial.
abstract.cn: 想象仪表指针停在一个刻度上。

sensesIntro.en: Place, time and rate are all treated as single points.

senses.title: Competitor in sport
senses.definition: a person who competes in a sport, especially one who trains hard
senses.definitionCN: 参加体育比赛、尤其经过刻苦训练的人
senses.example: The athlete trained for months before the race.
senses.exampleCN: 这名运动员赛前训练了几个月。

senses.title: Strong trained body
senses.definition: a person with a strong, fit and well-trained body
senses.definitionCN: 身材健壮、训练有素的人

senses.why: Since contenders are visibly fit, the word stretched from the competitor to anyone built and trained like one.
senses.whyCN: 参赛者通常体格出众，于是这个词从「参赛的人」扩展到「像运动员那样健壮的人」。

intro.en: Athlete is a Greek word for a contender, and its root names the prize itself.
intro.cn: athlete 是希腊语中表示竞争者的人，词根指的正是奖品。

items.en: athlon meant 'prize or contest'.
items.cn: athlon 意为「奖品、竞赛」。

items.en: athletes meant 'one who contends for a prize'.
items.cn: athletes 意为「为奖品而竞争的人」。

items.en: athleta kept the sporting sense.

items.en: English athlete named a competitor in games.
items.cn: 英语 athlete 指竞技比赛中的选手。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the athlet stem; the near-meaning group names sports people.

entries.definition: one who runs in a race

normalIntro.cn: athlete 是为奖品而训练的人，不只是活动身体的人。

normal.en: The th is pronounced as a plain t sound in many accents.
normal.cn: 在许多口音里 th 读作普通的 t 音。

normal.en: The adjective is athletic, the field is athletics.
normal.cn: 形容词是 athletic，田径运动是 athletics。

normal.en: It is countable: an athlete, two athletes.
normal.cn: 它可数：一名运动员、两名运动员。

normal.en: Not every fit person is an athlete in the strict sense.
normal.cn: 严格说来，体格好的人不一定都是运动员。

normal.en: The final -e is silent.
normal.cn: 词尾的 e 不发音。

abstract.en: See a foot pressed against a starting block.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚抵住起跑器。

abstract.en: See a medal held up above a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象人群上方举起一枚奖牌。

abstract.en: See a body hardened by years of morning runs.
abstract.cn: 想象常年晨跑练出的身体。

examples.en: The athlete trained for months before the race.
examples.cn: 这名运动员赛前训练了几个月。

examples.en: Her brother is a natural athlete.
examples.cn: 她弟弟天生体格强健。

examples.en: Every athlete on the team passed the fitness test.
examples.cn: 队里每名运动员都通过了体能测试。

dict_mnemonic.text: 词根 athlon 是「奖品、竞赛」：为奖品而竞争的人是运动员；长期训练出来的健壮体格，也被称作 athlete。

root: 源自希腊语 athlon「奖品、竞赛」与 athletes「为奖品而竞争的人」，经拉丁语 athleta 进入英语；本指参赛选手，后也形容体格健壮的人。

sensesIntro.en: The contender and the trained body are two sides of the same sporting life.
sensesIntro.cn: 参赛者与训练出来的身体，是同一种运动生涯的两面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body set at the start line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具身体伏在起跑线上。

intro.en: The athl root, 'contest', also appears in the names of multi-event sports.
intro.cn: 词根 athl 意为竞赛，也出现在多项赛事的名称里。

latinIntro.en: Greek athlon passed through Latin athleta into English and into athletic vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 athlon 经拉丁语 athleta 进入英语，形成一整套体育词汇。

items.meaning: one who contends for a prize

definition_zh: 运动的；运动员的；体格健壮的；擅长体育的
definition_en: physically strong, fit and good at sports, or relating to sports and exercise
core_image: 一个肌肉线条分明的人在跑道上轻快地跨过栏架
scene: 体育课上老师夸奖道：You have become strong and athletic after two years of training, always first in every race.
sceneCN: 这里指「体格健壮、擅长运动」（第 2 个义项：形容人身体强健、擅长体育）；句意为经过两年训练，你变得如此健壮敏捷。

pos.zh: 运动的；体育的；体格健壮的；擅长运动的

senses.title: Relating to sports and exercise
senses.definition: connected with sports, games and physical exercise
senses.definitionCN: 与体育、竞赛和身体锻炼有关的
senses.example: The school built a new athletic field last summer.
senses.exampleCN: 学校去年夏天建了新的运动场。
senses.why: Athletic first attaches itself to things: fields, shoes, programs — anything that belongs to the world of sport.
senses.whyCN: athletic 最早附着在事物上：运动场、运动鞋、体育项目——一切属于体育世界的东西。

senses.title: Physically strong and fit
senses.definition: having a strong, healthy body and moving well, like a trained sports person
senses.definitionCN: 身体强壮健康、动作协调，像受过训练的运动员那样
senses.example: Years of swimming kept her tall and athletic.
senses.exampleCN: 多年游泳让她身材高挑、体格健壮。
senses.why: When applied to a person, athletic paints the body an athlete would have: strong, lean, quick.
senses.whyCN: 当 athletic 用在人身上时，描绘的是运动员才有的身体：强壮、精瘦、敏捷。

senses.title: Good at sports
senses.definition: skillful at running, jumping and playing sports
senses.definitionCN: 擅长跑、跳及各类体育运动
senses.example: He is athletic and can play almost any ball game well.
senses.exampleCN: 他运动天赋好，几乎什么球类都打得好。
senses.why: Beyond the body, athletic also credits the ability: someone who wins at sports is called athletic.
senses.whyCN: 除了身体本身，athletic 也称赞能力：在运动中胜出的人常被称为 athletic。

senses.title: Active and energetic in style
senses.definition: describing clothes or designs made for movement and comfort
senses.definitionCN: 形容为方便活动、舒适而设计的服装或风格
senses.example: Athletic wear is now common on city streets, not only in gyms.
senses.exampleCN: 运动风服装如今常见于街头，不再只出现在健身房。
senses.why: Fashion borrowed the word for anything that suggests motion, sweat and freedom of movement.
senses.whyCN: 时尚界借用了这个词，形容一切暗示运动、流汗与活动自由的设计。

intro.en: athletic comes from Greek athletes (contestant) via athlete, with the English adjective suffix -ic.
intro.cn: athletic 来自希腊语 athletes（竞技者），经由 athlete 加英语形容词后缀 -ic 构成。

items.en: Greek athlon meant 'contest, prize'; athletes meant someone who competed for a prize.
items.cn: 希腊语 athlon 意为「竞赛、奖赏」；athletes 指为奖赏而竞赛的人。

items.en: Latin borrowed athleta for the competitor in public games.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 athleta，指公开竞技中的选手。

items.en: French athlétique carried the adjective sense into European learned vocabulary.
items.cn: 法语 athlétique 把形容词义带进欧洲学术词汇。

items.en: English athletic appears in the 1650s, first describing the games and exercises of ancient athletes.
items.cn: 英语 athletic 出现于 1650 年代，最初形容古代竞技者的比赛与操练。

items.en: From the 19th century athletic expanded to modern sports culture, sportswear and body type.
items.cn: 19 世纪起 athletic 扩展到现代体育文化、运动服装与体格描述。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root athl- family; group two holds near-meaning fitness adjectives.
note.cn: 第一组是同属 athl- 词根的词族；第二组是语义相近的体格类形容词。

entries.definition: The person who does sports; athletic is the adjective for that person or that world.
entries.definitionCN: 做运动的人；athletic 是形容该人或该领域的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for track and field sports; athletic describes, athletics names.
entries.definitionCN: 田径运动的名词；athletic 作描述，athletics 作名称。

entries.definition: The adverb: moves athletically means moves like a trained sports person.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式：动得 athletically 指动作像运动员一样。

entries.definition: Informal word for someone who likes or is good at sports; lighter than athletic.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中形容爱运动或擅长运动的人；比 athletic 更随意。

entries.definition: Describes big muscles only, without the skill side that athletic includes.
entries.definitionCN: 只形容肌肉发达，不含 athletic 所带的运动能力。

entries.definition: Healthy and in shape; broader than athletic, which also implies sports skill.
entries.definitionCN: 健康有型；范围比 athletic 广，但不强调运动技能。

normalIntro.en: athletic is simply athlete + -ic: everything that belongs to the athlete.
normalIntro.cn: athletic 就是 athlete + -ic：一切属于运动员的东西。

normal.en: athlete is inside the word: an athletic body looks like an athlete's body.
normal.cn: athlete 藏在词里：athletic 的身材就像运动员的身材。

normal.en: -ic turns nouns into adjectives, as in hero → heroic.
normal.cn: -ic 把名词变成形容词，如 hero → heroic。

normal.en: athletics (track and field) is the noun family member.
normal.cn: athletics（田径）是这个词族的名词成员。

normal.en: Greek athlon means prize: athletes once competed for prizes.
normal.cn: 希腊语 athlon 意为奖赏：athletes 原本就是为奖赏而赛的人。

normal.en: athletic shoes are shoes made for athletes.
normal.cn: athletic shoes 就是为运动员设计的鞋。

abstract.en: A chalk-dusted hand gripping a pull-up bar at dawn.
abstract.cn: 清晨，一只沾满镁粉的手握住单杠。

abstract.en: The lean silhouette of a runner against rising sun.
abstract.cn: 朝阳下奔跑者精瘦的剪影。

abstract.en: The springy feeling in legs after months of training.
abstract.cn: 数月训练后双腿弹性的感觉。

examples.en: Regular training made the whole rowing team strong and athletic.
examples.cn: 常年训练让整支赛艇队强壮而有运动能力。

examples.en: She wore her athletic gear even on rest days.
examples.cn: 她休息日也穿着运动装。

examples.en: The college offers athletic scholarships to talented runners.
examples.cn: 这所大学为有天赋的跑步选手提供体育奖学金。

dict_mnemonic.text: athlete（运动员）+ -ic（形容词后缀）= 运动员的；健壮的

root: 希腊语 athlon（竞赛、奖赏）→ athletes（竞技者）→ athlete → + -ic → athletic。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses spread from the athlete's world: things connected to sport, the strong body, the sports skill, and an energetic design style.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项围绕运动员的世界展开：与体育相关的事物、强健的体格、运动能力，以及充满力量感的设计风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lean runner clearing a hurdle in one smooth stride.
core.cn: 核心意象：精瘦的跑者一步流畅地跨过栏架。

branches.en: THINGS OF SPORT: fields, shoes, programs tied to exercise.
branches.cn: 体育之物：运动场、运动鞋、体育项目等与锻炼相关的事物。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a strong body and the ability to play sports well.
branches.cn: 人本身：强健的身体和良好的运动能力。

branches.en: DESIGN: clothing and styles built for movement.
branches.cn: 设计：为活动而生的服装与风格。

branches.en: BODY TYPE: the athlete-like figure people train for.
branches.cn: 体格：人们锻炼所追求的运动员式身材。

branches.en: ENERGY: speed, power and freedom of movement in life and fashion.
branches.cn: 活力：生活与时尚中的速度、力量与活动自由。

intro.en: athletic is athlete + -ic; the Greek root athl- (contest) also gives athlete, athletics and biathlon.

latinIntro.en: The root athl- is Greek, borrowed into Latin as athleta, then into European languages.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 athl- 来自希腊语，拉丁语借为 athleta，之后进入欧洲各语言。

senses.title: Track and field sports
senses.definition: the group of sports including running, jumping, throwing and walking events
senses.definitionCN: 包括跑、跳、投、竞走等项目的运动总称
senses.example: She takes part in athletics every weekend during the season.
senses.exampleCN: 赛季期间她每周末都参加田径运动。
senses.why: British English groups all track and field events under one plural-looking name, athletics.
senses.whyCN: 英式英语把所有田径项目归到一个带 -s 的名称之下：athletics。

senses.title: Competitive sports in general
senses.definition: organized competitive sports at a school, college or national level
senses.definitionCN: 学校、大学或国家层面组织的竞技体育活动
senses.example: The university invests heavily in its athletics program.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学在竞技体育项目上投入巨大。

senses.title: Physical exercise as a study or practice
senses.titleCN: 作为学科或实践的体育

senses.definitionCN: 对体育锻炼与训练的研究或实践
senses.example: He studied athletics and coaching at the sports institute.
senses.exampleCN: 他在体育学院学习体育学与教练课程。
senses.why: As a singular academic subject, athletics names the field of knowledge about sport.
senses.whyCN: 作单数的学科名称时，athletics 指关于体育的知识领域。

intro.en: athletics is the English plural-style noun from athletic, on Greek athlon (contest), referring to the whole set of contests.
intro.cn: athletics 是由 athletic 构成的带 -s 形式的英语名词，源自希腊语 athlon（竞赛），指整套竞技项目。

items.en: Greek athlon meant 'contest, prize'; athletes meant prize contestant.
items.cn: 希腊语 athlon 意为「竞赛、奖赏」；athletes 指争夺奖赏的选手。

items.en: Latin athleta kept the competitor sense in public games.
items.cn: 拉丁语 athleta 保留了公开竞技选手的含义。

items.en: English athletics appeared in the 17th century for the exercises and contests of ancient athletes.
items.cn: 英语 athletics 于 17 世纪出现，指古代竞技者的操练与比赛。

items.en: In the 19th century, athletics became the standard British name for track and field sports.
items.cn: 19 世纪维多利亚时代，athletics 成为英式田径运动的标准名称。

items.en: In American English, athletics broadened to mean the entire competitive sports program of an institution.

note.en: Group one collects the same-root athl- family; group two collects near-meaning sports nouns.
note.cn: 第一组是同属 athl- 词根的词族；第二组是语义相近的体育类名词。

entries.definition: The individual competitor; athletics is the set of sports they compete in.
entries.definitionCN: 参赛的个人；athletics 是他们所参加的运动总称。

entries.definition: The adjective without -s; describes bodies, shoes and programs.
entries.definitionCN: 不带 -s 的形容词；形容体格、运动鞋与体育项目。

entries.definition: Ends in -ics like athletics but means balancing and tumbling acts, a different sport family.
entries.definitionCN: 与 athletics 同以 -ics 结尾，但指平衡与翻腾技巧，属不同运动门类。

entries.definition: The American name for the same running, jumping and throwing events.
entries.definitionCN: 美式对同一批跑、跳、投项目的称呼。

entries.definition: Any single game or physical contest; athletics is the collective field.
entries.definitionCN: 任一单项运动；athletics 是运动的总领域。

entries.definition: Another -ics sport name, focused on apparatus and floor exercises.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个 -ics 运动名，专注器械与自由体操。

normalIntro.en: athletics is athletic + -s: the whole family of athletic contests under one name.
normalIntro.cn: athletics 是 athletic + -s：把所有竞技项目收进一个名字。

normal.en: athlete lives inside it: athletics is what athletes do.
normal.cn: 词里有 athlete：athletics 就是运动员做的事。

normal.en: It looks plural but takes a singular verb: athletics is popular.
normal.cn: 形式像复数但谓语用单数：athletics is popular。

normal.en: British athletics equals American track and field.
normal.cn: 英式 athletics 相当于美式 track and field。

normal.en: -ics endings often name fields: physics, economics, athletics.
normal.cn: -ics 结尾常表学科领域：physics、economics、athletics。

normal.en: Picture a stadium with running track, jumping pits and throwing circles.
normal.cn: 想象一座有跑道、沙坑和投掷圈的体育场。

abstract.en: A starting gun's echo hanging over a silent stadium.

abstract.cn: 红色跑道上白色的道次编号，笔直向前。

examples.en: The school's athletics day brings together all the track events.
examples.cn: 学校的运动会把所有田径项目聚在一起。

examples.en: He broke two national athletics records in one season.
examples.cn: 他一个赛季打破了两项全国田径纪录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red running track where runners, jumpers and throwers all compete.

branches.en: TRACK AND FIELD: running, jumping and throwing as one named set.
branches.cn: 田径：跑、跳、投构成的总称。

branches.en: SPORTS PROGRAMS: the competitive system of a school or nation.
branches.cn: 体育项目体系：学校或国家的竞技体系。

branches.en: STUDY: physical training as an academic subject.
branches.cn: 学科：作为研究对象的体育训练。

branches.en: COMPETITION: from school meets to national championships.
branches.cn: 竞赛：从校运会到全国锦标赛。

branches.en: ORGANIZATION: the people and institutions that run sports.
branches.cn: 组织：管理体育的人与机构。

intro.en: athletics adds the collective -s to athletic; the athl- root (contest) also builds athlete, biathlon and decathlon.
intro.cn: athletics 在 athletic 上加集合性的 -s；athl- 词根（竞赛）还构成 athlete、biathlon、decathlon。

latinIntro.en: athl- is Greek for contest, passed through Latin athleta into modern sports vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: athl- 是希腊语的「竞赛」，经拉丁语 athleta 进入现代体育词汇。
